Evan Ferguson (ankle), Yankuba Minteh (leg), Mats Wieffer (knee), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) all remain out, while Femi Azeez (hamstring) has had some "minor issues" after a mid-season friendly and may not be risked. It's otherwise positive news, with Lewis Dunk returning from a stiff neck, Jack Hinshelwood (unspecified) training this week and potentially rejoining the bench, Yasin Ayari recovering from illness, and Charalampos Kostoulas shaking off a knock he suffered while away with Greece. We didn't get an update on Pascal Struijk (hamstring) but Fabian Hurzeler did talk in terms of having "four really good centre-backs" available, so we assume he's fine. Speaking of Struijk, he may be the unlucky party to make way with club captain Dunk back available. Other than that, it's hard to envisage too many changes after a superb 3-0 win over Arsenal. The more physical Chema Andres may again be preferred over Malick Yalcouye, given that Sunderland's robust midfield bullied Declan Rice and co in the Black Cats' last home game, while Kostoulas should again get the nod over Georginio Rutter, despite the latter having his "best training week ever" over the break. Luka Vuskovic racked up the most international minutes of any Brighton outfielder over the last fortnight, and was one of the few Albion assets in midweek action, but Hurzeler hasn't rested him in *any* competition at all this season.

In a big boost for Chelsea and many FPL managers, Joao Pedro (knee), Reece James (hamstring), Cole Palmer (muscle), Marco Palestra (quad) and Moises Caicedo (calf) have trained and are “ready to go”. The only player on the sidelines, then, is Jamie Gittens, who will be out for a few weeks with an ankle issue picked up over the break. Being available and being ready to start are two different things, of course, and it'll be interesting to see just how many of the above quintet actually make the teamsheet on Saturday; we're learning more about Xabi Alonso's dependability, or lack of it, by the week. Alonso did suggest that Chelsea did "not take risks" with Caicedo against Brentford three weeks ago, so it sounds like he wasn't too far away even then. As for Palmer, the Chelsea boss says he has "trained the last week", and it sounds like his exit from the England camp was more precautionary in nature. Pedro isn't thought to have trained as long and had a bona fide injury before the break, so his starting chances may not be as great. Similarly, with Palestra, he hasn't featured at all competitively this season, so a start against a side as high-octane as Bournemouth may be a tall order. Romeo Lavia impressed with Belgium over the break and may stand a chance of starting in midfield, while Josh Acheampong is surely pushing for a recall after the defensive debacle from his three positional rivals in Gameweek 5.

Milan van Ewijk (hamstring) has returned to training and should feature, while Kaine Kesler-Hayden (hamstring) is also back on the grass – although he’s been unavailable for a longer period, so match fitness is likely an issue. Frank Lampard said all of his internationals have returned unscathed, meanwhile. That leaves Haji Wright (quad), Luke Woolfenden (knee), Josh Eccles (calf) and Aurele Amenda (calf) on the sidelines, while Taiwo Awoniyi serves the final game of a three-match domestic ban. Does Lampard embrace the 'never change a winning side' mantra this Monday, following Coventry's first Premier League victory of the campaign? The fit-again van Ewijk for makeshift wing-back Caleb Yirenkyi would be the most obvious change, if there is one, with Yirenkyi either dropping out or moving into midfield. Ephron Mason-Clark was hooked at half-time in Gameweek 5, so it's possible we could see him replaced. It may be too soon for a start for Yann Gboho but Loum Tchaouna, who came on for Mason-Clark at the City Ground, is an option. Brandon Thomas-Asante did quite a good job leading the line in Gameweek 5, so may well get the nod again against Newcastle.

Dean Henderson (ankle), Jean-Philippe Mateta (hamstring) and Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) are close to returns, with Mateta even back in training. The Nottingham Forest match comes too soon for that trio, however, with comebacks anticipated for next week instead. Chadi Riad (knee) is also out, while Axel Disasi continues to serve a three-game ban. Anan Khalaili (hamstring) is at least fit, despite a scare over the break, with his manager even saying that he is "ready to play 90 minutes". Pierre Sage added that Ismaila Sarr, who returned as a substitute before the break, is also now ready to start games, and it'll be interesting to see if he does indeed crack the starting XI for the first time since his post-deadline-day sulk. Daichi Kamada or Yeremy Pino would have to make way for that to happen. At the back, it's a question of whether Jefferson Lerma (who came on at half-time to help Palace to a clean sheet at Leeds) or Honest Ahanor fills in for Tomiyasu. Sage may well deem playing Ahanor and Jaydee Canvot together as too much inexperience (he's yet to do it), and Jefferson Lerma's aerial prowess may be a handy weapon against a team as handy from set plays as Forest.

Vitalii Mykolenko (leg), who exited the Ukraine camp early after just one appearance, could yet feature this weekend, with David Moyes saying that he has "got a chance for Sunday" and that "the extra day might help". Christian Norgaard (groin), who featured in a friendly last Friday, may also be involved, but Moyes said he would ideally like to give him more time and it'll surely be substitute duty at best for the experienced Dane. There was no update on Merlin Rohl, who has been missing since Gameweek 3 with a minor issue. The last we heard, he was back on the grass and aiming for a Gameweek 6 return. With Moyes saying Norgaard might be needed with "numbers being so short", is he perhaps implying that his other three central midfielders will all start at the weekend, with James Garner needed at full-back? If so, Hayden Hackney could come in to the side, with Norgaard warming the bench as the only back-up for the engine room. Probably the only other question mark this week is, again, who starts on the right wing. Brennan Johnson keeps flattering to deceive and yet keeps getting picked regardless, leaving an improving Tyler Dibling and (admittedly on his wrong side) Tyrique George waiting in the wings.

Alvaro Arbeloa began his press conference by saying that, at present, he had everyone “fit and available”. Kenny Tete, who missed out in Gameweek 5 with a concussion, is among that number. The Fulham boss did, however, clarify that matchday involvement may be premature for Tom Cairney (knee), who missed the opening month of the season and who only returned to training over the break. Arbeloa also said that Antonee Robinson had “some issues with his ankle” but “thinks” he will be available, albeit with a decision to be made over whether he starts or contributes from the bench. Robinson also had the latest return from international duty of anyone in the Fulham squad, having played in the Americas, so it wouldn't be a total shock to see Ryan Sessegnon start. Tete may get a look-in on the other flank, too, given that Timothy Castagne racked up 360 minutes for Belgium in the last fortnight. Central midfield pair Sander Berge and Shea Charles likewise completed all four of their nations' games, but those two have been influential in Fulham's recent mini-renaissance. Arbeloa has indeed kept the same side in the recent draws with Liverpool and Man Utd, so any changes are probably going to be fitness-led rather than linked to form.

Charlie Hughes (groin), Jack Butland (shoulder), Matt Targett (ankle) and Ilyas Ansah (back) remain out. So too do Darko Gyabi (thigh) and Elliot Matazo (knee) but those two, along with Óscar Zambrano, aren’t in the 25-man Premier League squad anyway. Mohamed Ali-Cho is also a doubt. The good news is that Nobel Mendy is back from a concussion, while Brooke Norton-Cuffy (hamstring), Tim Iroegbunam (knee) and Hidemasa Morita (adductor) have returned to training. So too has Elliot Stroud, who exited the Sweden camp at the end of September with illness. Sergej Jakirovic did hint that match fitness may dent Iroegbunam and Morita's chances of starting, so it may be a straight fight in midfield between Lucas Gourna-Douath and Matt Crooks, the latter of whom was hooked at half-time against Newcastle. It'll also be interesting to see if Stroud reclaims the left-wing spot from Sorba Thomas, who failed to really grasp his chance in Gameweek 5. At the back, Mendy will likely come back in for Lucas Herrington. The other eight players in the starting XI not already mentioned in the text above are ever-present starters this season.

Gary O’Neil has a fully fit squad for the clash with Fulham. Central midfielder Jack Taylor (knee), who underwent post-season surgery in May, featured in a behind-closed-doors mid-season friendly last week and then got an hour in Tuesday’s EFL Trophy match with Peterborough, so he's the latest and last one out of the physio room. There is one absentee this weekend, however: Abdul Fatawu serves a one-match ban following his red card last time out. Who fills in for Fatawu is the big question. Sandre Walle Egeli and Kasey McAteer are probably the more natural options but neither player has had much of a look-in of late, so it may be that O'Neil switches one of his left-wingers to their less favoured flank. Jaden Philogene was the first man off the bench in Gameweek 5 and has the advantage of not going away with their country over the break, but it's also possible that Daizen Maeda is brought back into the fold against Fulham. In midfield, there's the option for O'Neil to go for Luis Florentino or Marcelino Nunez over Exequiel Palacios, who featured for Argentina in the early hours of Wednesday morning. And at the back, Jacob Greaves and Kjell Scherpen lost their places to Abdoul Ouattara and Christian Walton last time out.

Joe Rodon (hamstring) and forgotten man Mateo Joseph (knee) remain on the sidelines for the Whites, while Daniel James (back) has joined the injury list. In better news, Harry Wilson (quad) returned to training over the international break, and young winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya, who withdrew from the France under-21 squad with an ankle injury, could also make a swift return. A trip to 'Set Piece FC' might be a game for the physical Jaka Bijol. If the Slovenian does come in, it'll be interesting to see whether James Justin, Nico Elvedi or maybe even Jayden Bogle (Justin could play at right wing-back) makes way. Further forward, it wouldn't be a massive surprise to see fan 'un-favourite' Brenden Aaronson come in for a game such as this, potentially at the expense of Noah Okafor - although the Swiss winger's speed on the break is an asset in itself. Local site Leeds Live interestingly propose that Aaronson replaces Anton Stach, who has perhaps been off the boil a tad. In terms of international minutes, Elvedi, Bijol and Tarik Muharemovic each racked up a squad-high 360 of them over the last fortnight - but Farke will have to start at least two of them at centre-half. Ethan Ampadu also completed all four matches for Wales, and there seems little chance of him being rested.

Cody Gakpo (ankle) and Alexander Isak (quad) will both miss the clash with Manchester City. Andoni Iraola said neither injury looked "long-term", at least, and the pair will be assessed "day to day". Long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee) and, likely, Giovanni Leoni (knee) also remain out, although the latter is closing in on a return this month. Jeremy Jacquet (hamstring), another casualty of the last fortnight, has at least recovered and trained, and Federico Chiesa could be back from a muscle issue. It seems to be a straight enough picture with the in-form defence, especially with Jacquet getting the green light to return. All the question marks are further forward, then, and how Iraola replaces Isak and Gakpo. Lewis Koumas could well get a look-in, and Iraola said the youngster "has our trust", but it'd be a big ask for the 21-year-old striker to make his first Premier League start in a fixture of this magnitude. So, then, Iraola might instead go with one of his wingers through the middle (something he suggested as an alternative in his presser) or just maybe try to catch City out with a third option he didn't raise as a possibility, such as Florian Wirtz as a false nine or as part of a 'double 10' with Dominik Szoboszlai. This latter option could see Trey Nyoni or Ryan Gravenberch start alongside Alexis Mac Allister.

In a press conference predictably dominated by topics off the field, specifically the guilty verdict on City’s financial misconduct charges, Enzo Maresca was finally asked how Erling Haaland was. The Norwegian striker had requested to be substituted while playing for Norway last weekend but the signs then were that it was mere fatigue, and Maresca confirmed that the City forward is indeed fit to face Liverpool. There were no more team news questions, so we don’t have any more verbal updates on Nico O’Reilly and Antoine Semenyo. The former exited England’s camp midway through the break for “further assessment”, while Semenyo cited a “swollen leg” as the reason for his exit from the Ghana squad. Semenyo was, at least, seen in a training video earlier on Friday but we didn’t catch sight of O’Reilly, who could well have started this one. Phil Foden remains suspended, meanwhile. It'll be interesting to see if Maresca changes tack for this one after a barmy eight-goal thriller against Sunderland. Does he put Ayyoub Bouaddi into the engine room, for instance, and push Enzo Fernandez further forward? Or does the absence of Messrs Gakpo and Isak embolden him to go more attacking, with Rayan Cherki ahead of the midfield two? Jeremy Doku is also knocking on the door, although the Belgian winger hasn't started a game all season and may again have to make do with an impact role.

Benjamin Sesko (calf) and long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte (knee) remain out this weekend, and those two have been joined on the sidelines by Patrick Dorgu (hamstring) and, probably, Noussair Mazraoui (back), who pulled out of their respective national team squads midway through the break. Dorgu will be out for "a number of weeks", while Michael Carrick said Mazraoui is "not quite right yet". Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford also exited their countries’ camps but have "trained a little bit" since, along with Amad Diallo (unspecified), who hasn't featured all season. Carlos Baleba, an unused sub in Gameweek 5 on his return from an ankle issue, got minutes under his belt in last Friday’s friendly with Lausanne, and is "improving". There was no update on Matthijs de Ligt (back) and Tom Heaton (hamstring), who have been out all season, or Karl Darlow, who exited the Wales squad. The front four picks itself with Sesko and Dorgu out and Amad unlikely to be ready to feature, with Joshua Zirkzee an option if Rashford is still struggling. Meanwhile, probably the only way Baleba starts is if Mainoo isn't ready. Even then, Carrick has Mason Mount and Andrey Santos as fitter engine-room options.

Matthias Jaissle hopes to have “three or four” previously sidelined players back for the trip to Coventry City on Monday. Two of them are Joelinton (groin), who returned to training over the break, and Nico Gonzalez, who missed out in Gameweek 5 with a concussion. So, then, we may also see one or two more of Jacob Ramsey (thigh), Amar Dedic (hamstring), Anthony Elanga (unknown), Dan Burn (ankle), Will Osula (foot) and/or Tino Livramento (unspecified) back in Gameweek 6 - and the most recent training video suggests it could be Osula and Dedic. Back-up goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (hamstring) was the only real casualty of the international break, as Lewis Miley has returned to training after pulling out of the England under-21 squad. Sean Steur or Joe Willock may have to make way to accommodate the returning Gonzalez, while both could drop out if Dedic is fit and Miley reverts to midfield duties. Joelinton and Osula will very likely have to make do with substitute duty after so long out.

It looked like Forest were close to a clean bill of health, with Nicolo Savona (knee) the only absentee, but Oliver Glasner delivered a triple whammy of bad news on Friday. Igor Jesus is out for a few weeks with a calf issue, while Nikola Milenkovic, who only just returned from a hamstring injury in a mid-season friendly against Swansea City, is also back on the sidelines with a bone bruise. On top of that, Neco Williams is struggling with illness, something that prevented him from training on Friday. Williams at least has an extra day of recovery, with the game being played on Sunday, but Ola Aina and Luca Netz will be on standby to deputise if he fails to make it. Jair Cunha and Ousmane Diomande look set to stay in the side at the back with Milenkovic out, while Jesus' absence would seemingly cement Dan Ndoye's place in the starting XI. On international watch, Xaver Schlager did get four lots of 90 minutes for Austria, but with his nation finishing their Nations League ties early, it'll be a full week between his last international match and Gameweek 6. On a similar theme, the extra day will hopefully help late returnee Daniel Munoz in his recovery.

Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey (both hamstring) will miss out in Gameweek 6 after picking up injuries over the international break. Ballard's issue is the more serious of the two, with Brobbey potentially returning next week alongside Habib Diarra (hamstring). Romaine Mundle (knee) also remains on the sidelines but Reinildo is back from a ban and Noah Sadiki shook off a scare to feature for DR Congo in their final outing of the last fortnight. Wilson Isidor for Brobbey is a straight enough swap up top, while Reinildo will likely replace Dayann Methalie at left-back. Omar Alderete would seem to be the most natural replacement for Ballard at centre-back, too, but Regis Le Bris admitted that Alderete had had a difficult start to the season, and it's possible that Nordi Mukiele shifts over to centre-half and Trai Hume comes in at right-back. One argument against that is that Hume played a team-high 360 minutes for Northern Ireland over the break, although the last of those matches was on Monday.

Dutch centre-halves Micky van de Ven (hand) and Jan Paul van Hecke (foot) picked up issues over the break but Roberto De Zerbi says the two defenders are available for Saturday. So too is James Maddison, despite a small setback last week. De Zerbi did add that van Hecke’s wife had twins yesterday, however, and that he would have to "consider the emotional aspect"! Elsewhere, Pedro Porro (hamstring), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain unavailable, and Dejan Kulusevski (knee) will only travel with the squad to Old Trafford in a non-playing capacity. The Spurs boss also hinted that international minutes could be a factor, saying that the Lilywhites would "have to consider the many games in a row" for Andrew Robertson, van de Ven and Rodrigo Bentancur, the latter of whom also had a long trip back from India - although that match being played in Asia did mean that Bentancur would have played and returned earlier than he would have had the friendly been in the Americas. Lukewarm words from De Zerbi for Mateus Fernandes ("he needs time") also didn't signpost a first start in central midfield for the former Southampton and West Ham man. The Spurs boss very much did hint that Conor Gallagher would start in the '10' role, so it's probably just a question of which of Dominic Solanke, Mathys Tel or Mohammed Kudus fills the other attacking spot. Christos Tzolis (hamstring) will be out for “weeks” with an injury he picked up over the break, joining William Saliba (back) on the sidelines. Two more casualties of the last fortnight, Ezri Konsa (dead leg) and Kai Havertz (hamstring), face a late fitness test before Saturday ("we will see tomorrow"). Declan Rice also pulled out of international duty with England early in the break, with Mikel Arteta saying he has had “some issues” since the World Cup and that the Gunners “have to manage” him. The Arsenal boss is hopeful the midfielder will be available, however. Three squad members who Arteta definitely will be able to call on are Cristhian Mosquera (muscle), Ben White (groin) and Piero Hincapie (muscle), who have all returned to training over the break and are “available”. Max Dowman is fine, too, despite coming home early from England under-20 duty. Mosquera and Viktor Gyokeres are fairly straightforward stand-ins if Konsa and Havertz fail to recover, while Eberechi Eze surely deputises on the left in the absence of Tzolis. Aside from which of Jurrien Timber and White gets the nod at right-back, probably the main source of debate is what Arteta does in the engine room. Bruno Guimaraes was hooked early in the 0-3 loss to Brighton, while Rice's fitness status is uncertain. Myles Lewis-Skelly may well get a reprieve, then.

Modo Cisse (unspecified), long-term absentee Amadou Onana (knee) and Ian Maatsen (ankle) remain out for Aston Villa, and while Leon Goretzka (knee) is back in training, this match comes too soon for him. He could feature in Gameweek 7, instead. The good news for Villa is that Brian Madjo (ankle), Pau Torres (hamstring), Marco Bizot (back) and Alysson (unspecified) all featured in a mid-season kickabout with Sevilla last Friday. Madjo has been missing since pre-season, with the other three more recent absentees. Matty Cash, who picked up a knock while playing for Poland on Monday, has also trained. It'll be interesting to see whether Cash starts after four successive starts and a dead leg, while amassed game-time may also be a factor regarding Victor Lindelof and John McGinn, who were the only other Villans to start four matches over the break. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Taylor Harwood-Bellis may well fill in for Cash and Lindelof, while Ibrahim Mbaye could deputise for McGinn if needed. Alejandro Garnacho, who looked to be heading the way of Harvey Elliot, may also have played his way back into contention over the break with some strong mid-season friendly performances.

Marco Rose confirmed that Alex Scott (tendon) faces 4-5 weeks on the sidelines with the issue he picked up while away with England. Elsewhere, David Brooks seems to be fine, despite pulling out of the Wales squad at the end of September. And while the Chelsea game comes too soon for Justin Kluivert (muscle), Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), Amine Adli (calf), Eli Kroupi (foot) and Julian Araujo (thigh), they are all back on the grass, and some of them could return in the next week or two. As for who comes in for Scott, Rose has a few options: Lewis Cook, Alex Toth or even Alvaro Rodriguez. Cook and Tyler Adams together may be defensive overkill in the middle of the park but Rose has so far been reluctant to start Toth in any competition, even the EFL Cup. The bold move would be to drop Christie back to the 'eight' role and play Rodriguez with Evanilson, but that may be overly daring away at Chelsea, and the big-money summer signing still looks like he's adapting to English football. Outside of the three central midfield positions, every player is an ever-present starter this season. The good news is that no Bournemouth player got more than two starts on international duty, and while Adams did return late from the Americas, he was only a substitute in the USA's midweek win over Canada.

Keith Andrews confirmed that Antoni Milambo (knee) and Josh Dasilva (hamstring) remain out, along with Kaye Furo (knee), but he was vague with the rest of the team news. Asked about the recovering Sepp van den Berg (knee), Nathan Collins (calf) and Mathias Jensen (unknown), as well international break casualties Dango Ouattara (illness) and Mikkel Damsgaard (ankle), the Brentford boss said they'd all "been on the grass, been around training... and [are] getting close to a return". That may be manager-speak for 'close but not quite ready', and if so, Mamadou Sangare might find a route back into the side, with Andrews forced into the same central midfield three he used away at Bournemouth in Gameweek 4. Fabio Carvalho, who bagged the Bees' win-sealing goal off the bench against Chelsea, is an option in the '10' role, too. El Hadji Malick Diouf may have to bide his time again, meanwhile, with Keane Lewis-Potter part of a Brentford defence that shut out the free-scoring Blues in Gameweek 5.

The Fulham boss did, however, clarify that matchday involvement may be premature for Tom Cairney (knee), who missed the opening month of the season and who only returned to training over the break. Arbeloa also said that Antonee Robinson had “some issues with his ankle” but “thinks” he will be available, albeit with a decision to be made over whether he starts or contributes from the bench. Robinson also had the latest return from international duty of anyone in the Fulham squad, having played in the Americas, so it wouldn't be a total shock to see Ryan Sessegnon start. Tete may get a look-in on the other flank, too, given that Timothy Castagne racked up 360 minutes for Belgium in the last fortnight. Central midfield pair Sander Berge and Shea Charles likewise completed all four of their nations' games, but those two have been influential in Fulham's recent mini-renaissance. Arbeloa has indeed kept the same side in the recent draws with Liverpool and Man Utd, so any changes are probably going to be fitness-led rather than linked to form.

Charlie Hughes (groin), Jack Butland (shoulder), Matt Targett (ankle) and Ilyas Ansah (back) remain out. So too do Darko Gyabi (thigh) and Elliot Matazo (knee) but those two, along with Óscar Zambrano, aren’t in the 25-man Premier League squad anyway. Mohamed Ali-Cho is also a doubt. The good news is that Nobel Mendy is back from a concussion, while Brooke Norton-Cuffy (hamstring), Tim Iroegbunam (knee) and Hidemasa Morita (adductor) have returned to training. So too has Elliot Stroud, who exited the Sweden camp at the end of September with illness. Sergej Jakirovic did hint that match fitness may dent Iroegbunam and Morita's chances of starting, so it may be a straight fight in midfield between Lucas Gourna-Douath and Matt Crooks, the latter of whom was hooked at half-time against Newcastle. It'll also be interesting to see if Stroud reclaims the left-wing spot from Sorba Thomas, who failed to really grasp his chance in Gameweek 5. At the back, Mendy will likely come back in for Lucas Herrington. The other eight players in the starting XI not already mentioned in the text above are ever-present starters this season.

Gary O’Neil has a fully fit squad for the clash with Fulham. Central midfielder Jack Taylor (knee), who underwent post-season surgery in May, featured in a behind-closed-doors mid-season friendly last week and then got an hour in Tuesday’s EFL Trophy match with Peterborough, so he's the latest and last one out of the physio room. There is one absentee this weekend, however: Abdul Fatawu serves a one-match ban following his red card last time out. Who fills in for Fatawu is the big question. Sandre Walle Egeli and Kasey McAteer are probably the more natural options but neither player has had much of a look-in of late, so it may be that O'Neil switches one of his left-wingers to their less favoured flank. Jaden Philogene was the first man off the bench in Gameweek 5 and has the advantage of not going away with their country over the break, but it's also possible that Daizen Maeda is brought back into the fold against Fulham. In midfield, there's the option for O'Neil to go for Luis Florentino or Marcelino Nunez over Exequiel Palacios, who featured for Argentina in the early hours of Wednesday morning. And at the back, Jacob Greaves and Kjell Scherpen lost their places to Abdoul Ouattara and Christian Walton last time out.

Joe Rodon (hamstring) and forgotten man Mateo Joseph (knee) remain on the sidelines for the Whites, while Daniel James (back) has joined the injury list. In better news, Harry Wilson (quad) returned to training over the international break, and young winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya, who withdrew from the France under-21 squad with an ankle injury, could also make a swift return. A trip to 'Set Piece FC' might be a game for the physical Jaka Bijol. If the Slovenian does come in, it'll be interesting to see whether James Justin, Nico Elvedi or maybe even Jayden Bogle (Justin could play at right wing-back) makes way. Further forward, it wouldn't be a massive surprise to see fan 'un-favourite' Brenden Aaronson come in for a game such as this, potentially at the expense of Noah Okafor - although the Swiss winger's speed on the break is an asset in itself. Local site Leeds Live interestingly propose that Aaronson replaces Anton Stach, who has perhaps been off the boil a tad. In terms of international minutes, Elvedi, Bijol and Tarik Muharemovic each racked up a squad-high 360 of them over the last fortnight - but Farke will have to start at least two of them at centre-half. Ethan Ampadu also completed all four matches for Wales, and there seems little chance of him being rested.

Cody Gakpo (ankle) and Alexander Isak (quad) will both miss the clash with Manchester City. Andoni Iraola said neither injury looked "long-term", at least, and the pair will be assessed "day to day". Long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee) and, likely, Giovanni Leoni (knee) also remain out, although the latter is closing in on a return this month. Jeremy Jacquet (hamstring), another casualty of the last fortnight, has at least recovered and trained, and Federico Chiesa could be back from a muscle issue. It seems to be a straight enough picture with the in-form defence, especially with Jacquet getting the green light to return. All the question marks are further forward, then, and how Iraola replaces Isak and Gakpo. Lewis Koumas could well get a look-in, and Iraola said the youngster "has our trust", but it'd be a big ask for the 21-year-old striker to make his first Premier League start in a fixture of this magnitude. So, then, Iraola might instead go with one of his wingers through the middle (something he suggested as an alternative in his presser) or just maybe try to catch City out with a third option he didn't raise as a possibility, such as Florian Wirtz as a false nine or as part of a 'double 10' with Dominik Szoboszlai. This latter option could see Trey Nyoni or Ryan Gravenberch start alongside Alexis Mac Allister.

In a press conference predictably dominated by topics off the field, specifically the guilty verdict on City’s financial misconduct charges, Enzo Maresca was finally asked how Erling Haaland was. The Norwegian striker had requested to be substituted while playing for Norway last weekend but the signs then were that it was mere fatigue, and Maresca confirmed that the City forward is indeed fit to face Liverpool. There were no more team news questions, so we don’t have any more verbal updates on Nico O’Reilly and Antoine Semenyo. The former exited England’s camp midway through the break for “further assessment”, while Semenyo cited a “swollen leg” as the reason for his exit from the Ghana squad. Semenyo was, at least, seen in a training video earlier on Friday but we didn’t catch sight of O’Reilly, who could well have started this one. Phil Foden remains suspended, meanwhile. It'll be interesting to see if Maresca changes tack for this one after a barmy eight-goal thriller against Sunderland. Does he put Ayyoub Bouaddi into the engine room, for instance, and push Enzo Fernandez further forward? Or does the absence of Messrs Gakpo and Isak embolden him to go more attacking, with Rayan Cherki ahead of the midfield two? Jeremy Doku is also knocking on the door, although the Belgian winger hasn't started a game all season and may again have to make do with an impact role.

Benjamin Sesko (calf) and long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte (knee) remain out this weekend, and those two have been joined on the sidelines by Patrick Dorgu (hamstring) and, probably, Noussair Mazraoui (back), who pulled out of their respective national team squads midway through the break. Dorgu will be out for "a number of weeks", while Michael Carrick said Mazraoui is "not quite right yet". Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford also exited their countries’ camps but have "trained a little bit" since, along with Amad Diallo (unspecified), who hasn't featured all season. Carlos Baleba, an unused sub in Gameweek 5 on his return from an ankle issue, got minutes under his belt in last Friday’s friendly with Lausanne, and is "improving". There was no update on Matthijs de Ligt (back) and Tom Heaton (hamstring), who have been out all season, or Karl Darlow, who exited the Wales squad. The front four picks itself with Sesko and Dorgu out and Amad unlikely to be ready to feature, with Joshua Zirkzee an option if Rashford is still struggling. Meanwhile, probably the only way Baleba starts is if Mainoo isn't ready. Even then, Carrick has Mason Mount and Andrey Santos as fitter engine-room options.

Matthias Jaissle hopes to have “three or four” previously sidelined players back for the trip to Coventry City on Monday. Two of them are Joelinton (groin), who returned to training over the break, and Nico Gonzalez, who missed out in Gameweek 5 with a concussion. So, then, we may also see one or two more of Jacob Ramsey (thigh), Amar Dedic (hamstring), Anthony Elanga (unknown), Dan Burn (ankle), Will Osula (foot) and/or Tino Livramento (unspecified) back in Gameweek 6 - and the most recent training video suggests it could be Osula and Dedic. Back-up goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (hamstring) was the only real casualty of the international break, as Lewis Miley has returned to training after pulling out of the England under-21 squad. Sean Steur or Joe Willock may have to make way to accommodate the returning Gonzalez, while both could drop out if Dedic is fit and Miley reverts to midfield duties. Joelinton and Osula will very likely have to make do with substitute duty after so long out.

It looked like Forest were close to a clean bill of health, with Nicolo Savona (knee) the only absentee, but Oliver Glasner delivered a triple whammy of bad news on Friday. Igor Jesus is out for a few weeks with a calf issue, while Nikola Milenkovic, who only just returned from a hamstring injury in a mid-season friendly against Swansea City, is also back on the sidelines with a bone bruise. On top of that, Neco Williams is struggling with illness, something that prevented him from training on Friday. Williams at least has an extra day of recovery, with the game being played on Sunday, but Ola Aina and Luca Netz will be on standby to deputise if he fails to make it. Jair Cunha and Ousmane Diomande look set to stay in the side at the back with Milenkovic out, while Jesus' absence would seemingly cement Dan Ndoye's place in the starting XI. On international watch, Xaver Schlager did get four lots of 90 minutes for Austria, but with his nation finishing their Nations League ties early, it'll be a full week between his last international match and Gameweek 6. On a similar theme, the extra day will hopefully help late returnee Daniel Munoz in his recovery.

Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey (both hamstring) will miss out in Gameweek 6 after picking up injuries over the international break. Ballard's issue is the more serious of the two, with Brobbey potentially returning next week alongside Habib Diarra (hamstring). Romaine Mundle (knee) also remains on the sidelines but Reinildo is back from a ban and Noah Sadiki shook off a scare to feature for DR Congo in their final outing of the last fortnight. Wilson Isidor for Brobbey is a straight enough swap up top, while Reinildo will likely replace Dayann Methalie at left-back. Omar Alderete would seem to be the most natural replacement for Ballard at centre-back, too, but Regis Le Bris admitted that Alderete had had a difficult start to the season, and it's possible that Nordi Mukiele shifts over to centre-half and Trai Hume comes in at right-back. One argument against that is that Hume played a team-high 360 minutes for Northern Ireland over the break, although the last of those matches was on Monday.

Dutch centre-halves Micky van de Ven (hand) and Jan Paul van Hecke (foot) picked up issues over the break but Roberto De Zerbi says the two defenders are available for Saturday. So too is James Maddison, despite a small setback last week. De Zerbi did add that van Hecke’s wife had twins yesterday, however, and that he would have to "consider the emotional aspect"! Elsewhere, Pedro Porro (hamstring), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain unavailable, and Dejan Kulusevski (knee) will only travel with the squad to Old Trafford in a non-playing capacity. The Spurs boss also hinted that international minutes could be a factor, saying that the Lilywhites would "have to consider the many games in a row" for Andrew Robertson, van de Ven and Rodrigo Bentancur, the latter of whom also had a long trip back from India - although that match being played in Asia did mean that Bentancur would have played and returned earlier than he would have had the friendly been in the Americas. Lukewarm words from De Zerbi for Mateus Fernandes ("he needs time") also didn't signpost a first start in central midfield for the former Southampton and West Ham man. The Spurs boss very much did hint that Conor Gallagher would start in the '10' role, so it's probably just a question of which of Dominic Solanke, Mathys Tel or Mohammed Kudus fills the other attacking spot. Christos Tzolis (hamstring) will be out for “weeks” with an injury he picked up over the break, joining William Saliba (back) on the sidelines. Two more casualties of the last fortnight, Ezri Konsa (dead leg) and Kai Havertz (hamstring), face a late fitness test before Saturday ("we will see tomorrow"). Declan Rice also pulled out of international duty with England early in the break, with Mikel Arteta saying he has had “some issues” since the World Cup and that the Gunners “have to manage” him. The Arsenal boss is hopeful the midfielder will be available, however. Three squad members who Arteta definitely will be able to call on are Cristhian Mosquera (muscle), Ben White (groin) and Piero Hincapie (muscle), who have all returned to training over the break and are “available”. Max Dowman is fine, too, despite coming home early from England under-20 duty. Mosquera and Viktor Gyokeres are fairly straightforward stand-ins if Konsa and Havertz fail to recover, while Eberechi Eze surely deputises on the left in the absence of Tzolis. Aside from which of Jurrien Timber and White gets the nod at right-back, probably the main source of debate is what Arteta does in the engine room. Bruno Guimaraes was hooked early in the 0-3 loss to Brighton, while Rice's fitness status is uncertain. Myles Lewis-Skelly may well get a reprieve, then.

Modo Cisse (unspecified), long-term absentee Amadou Onana (knee) and Ian Maatsen (ankle) remain out for Aston Villa, and while Leon Goretzka (knee) is back in training, this match comes too soon for him. He could feature in Gameweek 7, instead. The good news for Villa is that Brian Madjo (ankle), Pau Torres (hamstring), Marco Bizot (back) and Alysson (unspecified) all featured in a mid-season kickabout with Sevilla last Friday. Madjo has been missing since pre-season, with the other three more recent absentees. Matty Cash, who picked up a knock while playing for Poland on Monday, has also trained. It'll be interesting to see whether Cash starts after four successive starts and a dead leg, while amassed game-time may also be a factor regarding Victor Lindelof and John McGinn, who were the only other Villans to start four matches over the break. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Taylor Harwood-Bellis may well fill in for Cash and Lindelof, while Ibrahim Mbaye could deputise for McGinn if needed. Alejandro Garnacho, who looked to be heading the way of Harvey Elliot, may also have played his way back into contention over the break with some strong mid-season friendly performances.

Marco Rose confirmed that Alex Scott (tendon) faces 4-5 weeks on the sidelines with the issue he picked up while away with England. Elsewhere, David Brooks seems to be fine, despite pulling out of the Wales squad at the end of September. And while the Chelsea game comes too soon for Justin Kluivert (muscle), Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), Amine Adli (calf), Eli Kroupi (foot) and Julian Araujo (thigh), they are all back on the grass, and some of them could return in the next week or two. As for who comes in for Scott, Rose has a few options: Lewis Cook, Alex Toth or even Alvaro Rodriguez. Cook and Tyler Adams together may be defensive overkill in the middle of the park but Rose has so far been reluctant to start Toth in any competition, even the EFL Cup. The bold move would be to drop Christie back to the 'eight' role and play Rodriguez with Evanilson, but that may be overly daring away at Chelsea, and the big-money summer signing still looks like he's adapting to English football. Outside of the three central midfield positions, every player is an ever-present starter this season. The good news is that no Bournemouth player got more than two starts on international duty, and while Adams did return late from the Americas, he was only a substitute in the USA's midweek win over Canada.

Keith Andrews confirmed that Antoni Milambo (knee) and Josh Dasilva (hamstring) remain out, along with Kaye Furo (knee), but he was vague with the rest of the team news. Asked about the recovering Sepp van den Berg (knee), Nathan Collins (calf) and Mathias Jensen (unknown), as well international break casualties Dango Ouattara (illness) and Mikkel Damsgaard (ankle), the Brentford boss said they'd all "been on the grass, been around training... and [are] getting close to a return". That may be manager-speak for 'close but not quite ready', and if so, Mamadou Sangare might find a route back into the side, with Andrews forced into the same central midfield three he used away at Bournemouth in Gameweek 4. Fabio Carvalho, who bagged the Bees' win-sealing goal off the bench against Chelsea, is an option in the '10' role, too. El Hadji Malick Diouf may have to bide his time again, meanwhile, with Keane Lewis-Potter part of a Brentford defence that shut out the free-scoring Blues in Gameweek 5.

Evan Ferguson (ankle), Yankuba Minteh (leg), Mats Wieffer (knee), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) all remain out, while Femi Azeez (hamstring) has had some "minor issues" after a mid-season friendly and may not be risked. It's otherwise positive news, with Lewis Dunk returning from a stiff neck, Jack Hinshelwood (unspecified) training this week and potentially rejoining the bench, Yasin Ayari recovering from illness, and Charalampos Kostoulas shaking off a knock he suffered while away with Greece. We didn't get an update on Pascal Struijk (hamstring) but Fabian Hurzeler did talk in terms of having "four really good centre-backs" available, so we assume he's fine. Speaking of Struijk, he may be the unlucky party to make way with club captain Dunk back available. Other than that, it's hard to envisage too many changes after a superb 3-0 win over Arsenal. The more physical Chema Andres may again be preferred over Malick Yalcouye, given that Sunderland's robust midfield bullied Declan Rice and co in the Black Cats' last home game, while Kostoulas should again get the nod over Georginio Rutter, despite the latter having his "best training week ever" over the break. Luka Vuskovic racked up the most international minutes of any Brighton outfielder over the last fortnight, and was one of the few Albion assets in midweek action, but Hurzeler hasn't rested him in *any* competition at all this season.

In a big boost for Chelsea and many FPL managers, Joao Pedro (knee), Reece James (hamstring), Cole Palmer (muscle), Marco Palestra (quad) and Moises Caicedo (calf) have trained and are “ready to go”. The only player on the sidelines, then, is Jamie Gittens, who will be out for a few weeks with an ankle issue picked up over the break. Being available and being ready to start are two different things, of course, and it'll be interesting to see just how many of the above quintet actually make the teamsheet on Saturday; we're learning more about Xabi Alonso's dependability, or lack of it, by the week. Alonso did suggest that Chelsea did "not take risks" with Caicedo against Brentford three weeks ago, so it sounds like he wasn't too far away even then. As for Palmer, the Chelsea boss says he has "trained the last week", and it sounds like his exit from the England camp was more precautionary in nature. Pedro isn't thought to have trained as long and had a bona fide injury before the break, so his starting chances may not be as great. Similarly, with Palestra, he hasn't featured at all competitively this season, so a start against a side as high-octane as Bournemouth may be a tall order. Romeo Lavia impressed with Belgium over the break and may stand a chance of starting in midfield, while Josh Acheampong is surely pushing for a recall after the defensive debacle from his three positional rivals in Gameweek 5.

Milan van Ewijk (hamstring) has returned to training and should feature, while Kaine Kesler-Hayden (hamstring) is also back on the grass – although he’s been unavailable for a longer period, so match fitness is likely an issue. Frank Lampard said all of his internationals have returned unscathed, meanwhile. That leaves Haji Wright (quad), Luke Woolfenden (knee), Josh Eccles (calf) and Aurele Amenda (calf) on the sidelines, while Taiwo Awoniyi serves the final game of a three-match domestic ban. Does Lampard embrace the 'never change a winning side' mantra this Monday, following Coventry's first Premier League victory of the campaign? The fit-again van Ewijk for makeshift wing-back Caleb Yirenkyi would be the most obvious change, if there is one, with Yirenkyi either dropping out or moving into midfield. Ephron Mason-Clark was hooked at half-time in Gameweek 5, so it's possible we could see him replaced. It may be too soon for a start for Yann Gboho but Loum Tchaouna, who came on for Mason-Clark at the City Ground, is an option. Brandon Thomas-Asante did quite a good job leading the line in Gameweek 5, so may well get the nod again against Newcastle.

Dean Henderson (ankle), Jean-Philippe Mateta (hamstring) and Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) are close to returns, with Mateta even back in training. The Nottingham Forest match comes too soon for that trio, however, with comebacks anticipated for next week instead. Chadi Riad (knee) is also out, while Axel Disasi continues to serve a three-game ban. Anan Khalaili (hamstring) is at least fit, despite a scare over the break, with his manager even saying that he is "ready to play 90 minutes". Pierre Sage added that Ismaila Sarr, who returned as a substitute before the break, is also now ready to start games, and it'll be interesting to see if he does indeed crack the starting XI for the first time since his post-deadline-day sulk. Daichi Kamada or Yeremy Pino would have to make way for that to happen. At the back, it's a question of whether Jefferson Lerma (who came on at half-time to help Palace to a clean sheet at Leeds) or Honest Ahanor fills in for Tomiyasu. Sage may well deem playing Ahanor and Jaydee Canvot together as too much inexperience (he's yet to do it), and Jefferson Lerma's aerial prowess may be a handy weapon against a team as handy from set plays as Forest.

Vitalii Mykolenko (leg), who exited the Ukraine camp early after just one appearance, could yet feature this weekend, with David Moyes saying that he has "got a chance for Sunday" and that "the extra day might help". Christian Norgaard (groin), who featured in a friendly last Friday, may also be involved, but Moyes said he would ideally like to give him more time and it'll surely be substitute duty at best for the experienced Dane. There was no update on Merlin Rohl, who has been missing since Gameweek 3 with a minor issue. The last we heard, he was back on the grass and aiming for a Gameweek 6 return. With Moyes saying Norgaard might be needed with "numbers being so short", is he perhaps implying that his other three central midfielders will all start at the weekend, with James Garner needed at full-back? If so, Hayden Hackney could come in to the side, with Norgaard warming the bench as the only back-up for the engine room. Probably the only other question mark this week is, again, who starts on the right wing. Brennan Johnson keeps flattering to deceive and yet keeps getting picked regardless, leaving an improving Tyler Dibling and (admittedly on his wrong side) Tyrique George waiting in the wings.

The former exited England’s camp midway through the break for “further assessment”, while Semenyo cited a “swollen leg” as the reason for his exit from the Ghana squad. Semenyo was, at least, seen in a training video earlier on Friday but we didn’t catch sight of O’Reilly, who could well have started this one. Phil Foden remains suspended, meanwhile. It'll be interesting to see if Maresca changes tack for this one after a barmy eight-goal thriller against Sunderland. Does he put Ayyoub Bouaddi into the engine room, for instance, and push Enzo Fernandez further forward? Or does the absence of Messrs Gakpo and Isak embolden him to go more attacking, with Rayan Cherki ahead of the midfield two? Jeremy Doku is also knocking on the door, although the Belgian winger hasn't started a game all season and may again have to make do with an impact role.

Benjamin Sesko (calf) and long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte (knee) remain out this weekend, and those two have been joined on the sidelines by Patrick Dorgu (hamstring) and, probably, Noussair Mazraoui (back), who pulled out of their respective national team squads midway through the break. Dorgu will be out for "a number of weeks", while Michael Carrick said Mazraoui is "not quite right yet". Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford also exited their countries’ camps but have "trained a little bit" since, along with Amad Diallo (unspecified), who hasn't featured all season. Carlos Baleba, an unused sub in Gameweek 5 on his return from an ankle issue, got minutes under his belt in last Friday’s friendly with Lausanne, and is "improving". There was no update on Matthijs de Ligt (back) and Tom Heaton (hamstring), who have been out all season, or Karl Darlow, who exited the Wales squad. The front four picks itself with Sesko and Dorgu out and Amad unlikely to be ready to feature, with Joshua Zirkzee an option if Rashford is still struggling. Meanwhile, probably the only way Baleba starts is if Mainoo isn't ready. Even then, Carrick has Mason Mount and Andrey Santos as fitter engine-room options.

Matthias Jaissle hopes to have “three or four” previously sidelined players back for the trip to Coventry City on Monday. Two of them are Joelinton (groin), who returned to training over the break, and Nico Gonzalez, who missed out in Gameweek 5 with a concussion. So, then, we may also see one or two more of Jacob Ramsey (thigh), Amar Dedic (hamstring), Anthony Elanga (unknown), Dan Burn (ankle), Will Osula (foot) and/or Tino Livramento (unspecified) back in Gameweek 6 - and the most recent training video suggests it could be Osula and Dedic. Back-up goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (hamstring) was the only real casualty of the international break, as Lewis Miley has returned to training after pulling out of the England under-21 squad. Sean Steur or Joe Willock may have to make way to accommodate the returning Gonzalez, while both could drop out if Dedic is fit and Miley reverts to midfield duties. Joelinton and Osula will very likely have to make do with substitute duty after so long out.

It looked like Forest were close to a clean bill of health, with Nicolo Savona (knee) the only absentee, but Oliver Glasner delivered a triple whammy of bad news on Friday. Igor Jesus is out for a few weeks with a calf issue, while Nikola Milenkovic, who only just returned from a hamstring injury in a mid-season friendly against Swansea City, is also back on the sidelines with a bone bruise. On top of that, Neco Williams is struggling with illness, something that prevented him from training on Friday. Williams at least has an extra day of recovery, with the game being played on Sunday, but Ola Aina and Luca Netz will be on standby to deputise if he fails to make it. Jair Cunha and Ousmane Diomande look set to stay in the side at the back with Milenkovic out, while Jesus' absence would seemingly cement Dan Ndoye's place in the starting XI. On international watch, Xaver Schlager did get four lots of 90 minutes for Austria, but with his nation finishing their Nations League ties early, it'll be a full week between his last international match and Gameweek 6. On a similar theme, the extra day will hopefully help late returnee Daniel Munoz in his recovery.

Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey (both hamstring) will miss out in Gameweek 6 after picking up injuries over the international break. Ballard's issue is the more serious of the two, with Brobbey potentially returning next week alongside Habib Diarra (hamstring). Romaine Mundle (knee) also remains on the sidelines but Reinildo is back from a ban and Noah Sadiki shook off a scare to feature for DR Congo in their final outing of the last fortnight. Wilson Isidor for Brobbey is a straight enough swap up top, while Reinildo will likely replace Dayann Methalie at left-back. Omar Alderete would seem to be the most natural replacement for Ballard at centre-back, too, but Regis Le Bris admitted that Alderete had had a difficult start to the season, and it's possible that Nordi Mukiele shifts over to centre-half and Trai Hume comes in at right-back. One argument against that is that Hume played a team-high 360 minutes for Northern Ireland over the break, although the last of those matches was on Monday.

Dutch centre-halves Micky van de Ven (hand) and Jan Paul van Hecke (foot) picked up issues over the break but Roberto De Zerbi says the two defenders are available for Saturday. So too is James Maddison, despite a small setback last week. De Zerbi did add that van Hecke’s wife had twins yesterday, however, and that he would have to "consider the emotional aspect"! Elsewhere, Pedro Porro (hamstring), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain unavailable, and Dejan Kulusevski (knee) will only travel with the squad to Old Trafford in a non-playing capacity. The Spurs boss also hinted that international minutes could be a factor, saying that the Lilywhites would "have to consider the many games in a row" for Andrew Robertson, van de Ven and Rodrigo Bentancur, the latter of whom also had a long trip back from India - although that match being played in Asia did mean that Bentancur would have played and returned earlier than he would have had the friendly been in the Americas. Lukewarm words from De Zerbi for Mateus Fernandes ("he needs time") also didn't signpost a first start in central midfield for the former Southampton and West Ham man. The Spurs boss very much did hint that Conor Gallagher would start in the '10' role, so it's probably just a question of which of Dominic Solanke, Mathys Tel or Mohammed Kudus fills the other attacking spot. Christos Tzolis (hamstring) will be out for “weeks” with an injury he picked up over the break, joining William Saliba (back) on the sidelines. Two more casualties of the last fortnight, Ezri Konsa (dead leg) and Kai Havertz (hamstring), face a late fitness test before Saturday ("we will see tomorrow"). Declan Rice also pulled out of international duty with England early in the break, with Mikel Arteta saying he has had “some issues” since the World Cup and that the Gunners “have to manage” him. The Arsenal boss is hopeful the midfielder will be available, however. Three squad members who Arteta definitely will be able to call on are Cristhian Mosquera (muscle), Ben White (groin) and Piero Hincapie (muscle), who have all returned to training over the break and are “available”. Max Dowman is fine, too, despite coming home early from England under-20 duty. Mosquera and Viktor Gyokeres are fairly straightforward stand-ins if Konsa and Havertz fail to recover, while Eberechi Eze surely deputises on the left in the absence of Tzolis. Aside from which of Jurrien Timber and White gets the nod at right-back, probably the main source of debate is what Arteta does in the engine room. Bruno Guimaraes was hooked early in the 0-3 loss to Brighton, while Rice's fitness status is uncertain. Myles Lewis-Skelly may well get a reprieve, then.

Modo Cisse (unspecified), long-term absentee Amadou Onana (knee) and Ian Maatsen (ankle) remain out for Aston Villa, and while Leon Goretzka (knee) is back in training, this match comes too soon for him. He could feature in Gameweek 7, instead. The good news for Villa is that Brian Madjo (ankle), Pau Torres (hamstring), Marco Bizot (back) and Alysson (unspecified) all featured in a mid-season kickabout with Sevilla last Friday. Madjo has been missing since pre-season, with the other three more recent absentees. Matty Cash, who picked up a knock while playing for Poland on Monday, has also trained. It'll be interesting to see whether Cash starts after four successive starts and a dead leg, while amassed game-time may also be a factor regarding Victor Lindelof and John McGinn, who were the only other Villans to start four matches over the break. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Taylor Harwood-Bellis may well fill in for Cash and Lindelof, while Ibrahim Mbaye could deputise for McGinn if needed. Alejandro Garnacho, who looked to be heading the way of Harvey Elliot, may also have played his way back into contention over the break with some strong mid-season friendly performances.

Marco Rose confirmed that Alex Scott (tendon) faces 4-5 weeks on the sidelines with the issue he picked up while away with England. Elsewhere, David Brooks seems to be fine, despite pulling out of the Wales squad at the end of September. And while the Chelsea game comes too soon for Justin Kluivert (muscle), Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), Amine Adli (calf), Eli Kroupi (foot) and Julian Araujo (thigh), they are all back on the grass, and some of them could return in the next week or two. As for who comes in for Scott, Rose has a few options: Lewis Cook, Alex Toth or even Alvaro Rodriguez. Cook and Tyler Adams together may be defensive overkill in the middle of the park but Rose has so far been reluctant to start Toth in any competition, even the EFL Cup. The bold move would be to drop Christie back to the 'eight' role and play Rodriguez with Evanilson, but that may be overly daring away at Chelsea, and the big-money summer signing still looks like he's adapting to English football. Outside of the three central midfield positions, every player is an ever-present starter this season. The good news is that no Bournemouth player got more than two starts on international duty, and while Adams did return late from the Americas, he was only a substitute in the USA's midweek win over Canada.

Keith Andrews confirmed that Antoni Milambo (knee) and Josh Dasilva (hamstring) remain out, along with Kaye Furo (knee), but he was vague with the rest of the team news. Asked about the recovering Sepp van den Berg (knee), Nathan Collins (calf) and Mathias Jensen (unknown), as well international break casualties Dango Ouattara (illness) and Mikkel Damsgaard (ankle), the Brentford boss said they'd all "been on the grass, been around training... and [are] getting close to a return". That may be manager-speak for 'close but not quite ready', and if so, Mamadou Sangare might find a route back into the side, with Andrews forced into the same central midfield three he used away at Bournemouth in Gameweek 4. Fabio Carvalho, who bagged the Bees' win-sealing goal off the bench against Chelsea, is an option in the '10' role, too. El Hadji Malick Diouf may have to bide his time again, meanwhile, with Keane Lewis-Potter part of a Brentford defence that shut out the free-scoring Blues in Gameweek 5.

Evan Ferguson (ankle), Yankuba Minteh (leg), Mats Wieffer (knee), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) all remain out, while Femi Azeez (hamstring) has had some "minor issues" after a mid-season friendly and may not be risked. It's otherwise positive news, with Lewis Dunk returning from a stiff neck, Jack Hinshelwood (unspecified) training this week and potentially rejoining the bench, Yasin Ayari recovering from illness, and Charalampos Kostoulas shaking off a knock he suffered while away with Greece. We didn't get an update on Pascal Struijk (hamstring) but Fabian Hurzeler did talk in terms of having "four really good centre-backs" available, so we assume he's fine. Speaking of Struijk, he may be the unlucky party to make way with club captain Dunk back available. Other than that, it's hard to envisage too many changes after a superb 3-0 win over Arsenal. The more physical Chema Andres may again be preferred over Malick Yalcouye, given that Sunderland's robust midfield bullied Declan Rice and co in the Black Cats' last home game, while Kostoulas should again get the nod over Georginio Rutter, despite the latter having his "best training week ever" over the break. Luka Vuskovic racked up the most international minutes of any Brighton outfielder over the last fortnight, and was one of the few Albion assets in midweek action, but Hurzeler hasn't rested him in *any* competition at all this season.

In a big boost for Chelsea and many FPL managers, Joao Pedro (knee), Reece James (hamstring), Cole Palmer (muscle), Marco Palestra (quad) and Moises Caicedo (calf) have trained and are “ready to go”. The only player on the sidelines, then, is Jamie Gittens, who will be out for a few weeks with an ankle issue picked up over the break. Being available and being ready to start are two different things, of course, and it'll be interesting to see just how many of the above quintet actually make the teamsheet on Saturday; we're learning more about Xabi Alonso's dependability, or lack of it, by the week. Alonso did suggest that Chelsea did "not take risks" with Caicedo against Brentford three weeks ago, so it sounds like he wasn't too far away even then. As for Palmer, the Chelsea boss says he has "trained the last week", and it sounds like his exit from the England camp was more precautionary in nature. Pedro isn't thought to have trained as long and had a bona fide injury before the break, so his starting chances may not be as great. Similarly, with Palestra, he hasn't featured at all competitively this season, so a start against a side as high-octane as Bournemouth may be a tall order. Romeo Lavia impressed with Belgium over the break and may stand a chance of starting in midfield, while Josh Acheampong is surely pushing for a recall after the defensive debacle from his three positional rivals in Gameweek 5.

Milan van Ewijk (hamstring) has returned to training and should feature, while Kaine Kesler-Hayden (hamstring) is also back on the grass – although he’s been unavailable for a longer period, so match fitness is likely an issue. Frank Lampard said all of his internationals have returned unscathed, meanwhile. That leaves Haji Wright (quad), Luke Woolfenden (knee), Josh Eccles (calf) and Aurele Amenda (calf) on the sidelines, while Taiwo Awoniyi serves the final game of a three-match domestic ban. Does Lampard embrace the 'never change a winning side' mantra this Monday, following Coventry's first Premier League victory of the campaign? The fit-again van Ewijk for makeshift wing-back Caleb Yirenkyi would be the most obvious change, if there is one, with Yirenkyi either dropping out or moving into midfield. Ephron Mason-Clark was hooked at half-time in Gameweek 5, so it's possible we could see him replaced. It may be too soon for a start for Yann Gboho but Loum Tchaouna, who came on for Mason-Clark at the City Ground, is an option. Brandon Thomas-Asante did quite a good job leading the line in Gameweek 5, so may well get the nod again against Newcastle.

Dean Henderson (ankle), Jean-Philippe Mateta (hamstring) and Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) are close to returns, with Mateta even back in training. The Nottingham Forest match comes too soon for that trio, however, with comebacks anticipated for next week instead. Chadi Riad (knee) is also out, while Axel Disasi continues to serve a three-game ban. Anan Khalaili (hamstring) is at least fit, despite a scare over the break, with his manager even saying that he is "ready to play 90 minutes". Pierre Sage added that Ismaila Sarr, who returned as a substitute before the break, is also now ready to start games, and it'll be interesting to see if he does indeed crack the starting XI for the first time since his post-deadline-day sulk. Daichi Kamada or Yeremy Pino would have to make way for that to happen. At the back, it's a question of whether Jefferson Lerma (who came on at half-time to help Palace to a clean sheet at Leeds) or Honest Ahanor fills in for Tomiyasu. Sage may well deem playing Ahanor and Jaydee Canvot together as too much inexperience (he's yet to do it), and Jefferson Lerma's aerial prowess may be a handy weapon against a team as handy from set plays as Forest.

Vitalii Mykolenko (leg), who exited the Ukraine camp early after just one appearance, could yet feature this weekend, with David Moyes saying that he has "got a chance for Sunday" and that "the extra day might help". Christian Norgaard (groin), who featured in a friendly last Friday, may also be involved, but Moyes said he would ideally like to give him more time and it'll surely be substitute duty at best for the experienced Dane. There was no update on Merlin Rohl, who has been missing since Gameweek 3 with a minor issue. The last we heard, he was back on the grass and aiming for a Gameweek 6 return. With Moyes saying Norgaard might be needed with "numbers being so short", is he perhaps implying that his other three central midfielders will all start at the weekend, with James Garner needed at full-back? If so, Hayden Hackney could come in to the side, with Norgaard warming the bench as the only back-up for the engine room. Probably the only other question mark this week is, again, who starts on the right wing. Brennan Johnson keeps flattering to deceive and yet keeps getting picked regardless, leaving an improving Tyler Dibling and (admittedly on his wrong side) Tyrique George waiting in the wings.

Alvaro Arbeloa began his press conference by saying that, at present, he had everyone “fit and available”. Kenny Tete, who missed out in Gameweek 5 with a concussion, is among that number. The Fulham boss did, however, clarify that matchday involvement may be premature for Tom Cairney (knee), who missed the opening month of the season and who only returned to training over the break. Arbeloa also said that Antonee Robinson had “some issues with his ankle” but “thinks” he will be available, albeit with a decision to be made over whether he starts or contributes from the bench. Robinson also had the latest return from international duty of anyone in the Fulham squad, having played in the Americas, so it wouldn't be a total shock to see Ryan Sessegnon start. Tete may get a look-in on the other flank, too, given that Timothy Castagne racked up 360 minutes for Belgium in the last fortnight. Central midfield pair Sander Berge and Shea Charles likewise completed all four of their nations' games, but those two have been influential in Fulham's recent mini-renaissance. Arbeloa has indeed kept the same side in the recent draws with Liverpool and Man Utd, so any changes are probably going to be fitness-led rather than linked to form.

Charlie Hughes (groin), Jack Butland (shoulder), Matt Targett (ankle) and Ilyas Ansah (back) remain out. So too do Darko Gyabi (thigh) and Elliot Matazo (knee) but those two, along with Óscar Zambrano, aren’t in the 25-man Premier League squad anyway. Mohamed Ali-Cho is also a doubt. The good news is that Nobel Mendy is back from a concussion, while Brooke Norton-Cuffy (hamstring), Tim Iroegbunam (knee) and Hidemasa Morita (adductor) have returned to training. So too has Elliot Stroud, who exited the Sweden camp at the end of September with illness. Sergej Jakirovic did hint that match fitness may dent Iroegbunam and Morita's chances of starting, so it may be a straight fight in midfield between Lucas Gourna-Douath and Matt Crooks, the latter of whom was hooked at half-time against Newcastle. It'll also be interesting to see if Stroud reclaims the left-wing spot from Sorba Thomas, who failed to really grasp his chance in Gameweek 5. At the back, Mendy will likely come back in for Lucas Herrington. The other eight players in the starting XI not already mentioned in the text above are ever-present starters this season.

Gary O’Neil has a fully fit squad for the clash with Fulham. Central midfielder Jack Taylor (knee), who underwent post-season surgery in May, featured in a behind-closed-doors mid-season friendly last week and then got an hour in Tuesday’s EFL Trophy match with Peterborough, so he's the latest and last one out of the physio room. There is one absentee this weekend, however: Abdul Fatawu serves a one-match ban following his red card last time out. Who fills in for Fatawu is the big question. Sandre Walle Egeli and Kasey McAteer are probably the more natural options but neither player has had much of a look-in of late, so it may be that O'Neil switches one of his left-wingers to their less favoured flank. Jaden Philogene was the first man off the bench in Gameweek 5 and has the advantage of not going away with their country over the break, but it's also possible that Daizen Maeda is brought back into the fold against Fulham. In midfield, there's the option for O'Neil to go for Luis Florentino or Marcelino Nunez over Exequiel Palacios, who featured for Argentina in the early hours of Wednesday morning. And at the back, Jacob Greaves and Kjell Scherpen lost their places to Abdoul Ouattara and Christian Walton last time out.

Joe Rodon (hamstring) and forgotten man Mateo Joseph (knee) remain on the sidelines for the Whites, while Daniel James (back) has joined the injury list. In better news, Harry Wilson (quad) returned to training over the international break, and young winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya, who withdrew from the France under-21 squad with an ankle injury, could also make a swift return. A trip to 'Set Piece FC' might be a game for the physical Jaka Bijol. If the Slovenian does come in, it'll be interesting to see whether James Justin, Nico Elvedi or maybe even Jayden Bogle (Justin could play at right wing-back) makes way. Further forward, it wouldn't be a massive surprise to see fan 'un-favourite' Brenden Aaronson come in for a game such as this, potentially at the expense of Noah Okafor - although the Swiss winger's speed on the break is an asset in itself. Local site Leeds Live interestingly propose that Aaronson replaces Anton Stach, who has perhaps been off the boil a tad. In terms of international minutes, Elvedi, Bijol and Tarik Muharemovic each racked up a squad-high 360 of them over the last fortnight - but Farke will have to start at least two of them at centre-half. Ethan Ampadu also completed all four matches for Wales, and there seems little chance of him being rested.

Cody Gakpo (ankle) and Alexander Isak (quad) will both miss the clash with Manchester City. Andoni Iraola said neither injury looked "long-term", at least, and the pair will be assessed "day to day". Long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee) and, likely, Giovanni Leoni (knee) also remain out, although the latter is closing in on a return this month. Jeremy Jacquet (hamstring), another casualty of the last fortnight, has at least recovered and trained, and Federico Chiesa could be back from a muscle issue. It seems to be a straight enough picture with the in-form defence, especially with Jacquet getting the green light to return. All the question marks are further forward, then, and how Iraola replaces Isak and Gakpo. Lewis Koumas could well get a look-in, and Iraola said the youngster "has our trust", but it'd be a big ask for the 21-year-old striker to make his first Premier League start in a fixture of this magnitude. So, then, Iraola might instead go with one of his wingers through the middle (something he suggested as an alternative in his presser) or just maybe try to catch City out with a third option he didn't raise as a possibility, such as Florian Wirtz as a false nine or as part of a 'double 10' with Dominik Szoboszlai. This latter option could see Trey Nyoni or Ryan Gravenberch start alongside Alexis Mac Allister.
