Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) remain out, however. Shaw and Mainoo will surely start if fit, but with another Champions League tie on the horizon, risks may not be taken. Fernandes was deployed on the right against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday but will likely move back centrally here, potentially ousting Youri Tielemans from the ’10’. Marcus Rashford is an alternative to the wide options included here.

Anthony Elanga (unknown) remains out but could re-join training next week. Back-up goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (hamstring), Tino Livramento (unspecified) and Jacob Ramsey (thigh) will also miss Gameweek 7. If Gibbs-White fails to make it, Callum Hudson-Odoi is the most likely player to come in. At the back, Jair Cunha could replace Ola Aina, while Ibrahim Sangare is an alternative to James McAtee, should Glasner want more physicality in the middle of the park.

Trai Hume and Nilson Angulo could offer support from the flanks, with Malick Fofana another option out wide. Habib Diarra is an outside bet to start in one of the midfield positions, having recently returned from injury as a sub.

Frank Lampard used a 4-2-3-1 formation to beat Newcastle United on Monday, but may be tempted to revert to a back three for the trip to north London, a tactic he successfully used in the 1-0 away win over Nottingham Forest prior to the international break. In that scenario, Stephen Mfuni could come in for Ephron Mason-Clark. Sidiki Cherif’s goal in Gameweek 6 might see him continue up top, leaving Awoniyi and Ellis Simms in reserve.

Daichi Kamada came off the bench to score against Lyon in midweek and should return to the starting XI for Sunday’s trip to rivals Brighton and Hove Albion in the A23 derby. Adam Wharton has played back-to-back 90s but is expected to go again following his rest during the extended international break. Quinten Timber should keep his place alongside him. Yeremy Pino is in good form while a start for Ismaila Sarr is perhaps more likely in next Thursday’s Europa League match in Turkey. Elsewhere, Axel Disasi completes his suspension, with Colombian Jefferson Lerma continuing to cover in the back three. There was no update one way or the other on the current crop of injured players, with Pierre Sage using the words “potentially”, “hope”, and “expect” in his presser but ultimately admitting that he didn’t know. Walter Benitez impressed against Forest, although he then saved just one of five shots on target faced against Lyon. He still probably starts. Minutes off the bench for Jean-Philippe Mateta is probably the best owners can hope for. Positional rival Jorgen Strand Larsen came off just after the hour mark in France, so he should be fine for Sunday.

Vitalii Mykolenko (leg) could feature this weekend, with David Moyes saying he “is doing much better”. Jarrad Branthwaite (dead leg) may also be involved but faces a late fitness check. It sounds like Christian Norgaard will have to settle for a place on the bench again, however. As for the starting XI, Michael Keane will be on standby if any of the defenders miss out. Further forward, the usual question mark applies on the right wing. Brennan Johnson is hardly playing well at the moment yet keeps getting picked regardless, leaving Tyrique George waiting for his chance.

Hugo Larsson (groin) is a doubt, but Alvaro Arbeloa said everyone else is fit. That presumably includes Tom Cairney (knee), who returned to training over the international break, and Antonee Robinson, who missed out last week due to an ankle issue. With Robinson fit, he will likely return to the starting XI at the expense of Ryan Sessegnon. There could be a change on the opposite flank too, with Timothy Castagne in for Kenny Tete. Castagne was benched in Gameweek 6 but had racked up 360 minutes for Belgium over the international break. Further forward, Cesar Palacios is pushing for a recall.

Nobel Mendy has been ruled out for a couple of weeks with a groin problem, with Lucas Herrington his likely replacement on Saturday. Mohamed-Ali Cho (thigh) and Lucas Gourna-Douath (unknown) are also out but could return next week. Elsewhere, Matt Targett is out for two months with an ankle issue, joining Jack Butland (shoulder), Charlie Hughes (groin), Ilyas Ansah (back) and Darko Gyabi (thigh) on the sidelines. Sergej Jakirovic may be tempted to replace Matt Crooks with Tim Iroegbunam in central midfield, a change which occurred just after the hour mark last week. Further forward, Mohamed Belloumi should return to the starting XI, having previously been benched for fatigue following international duty. He’ll likely replace Joe Gelhardt, who Jakirovic said is still lacking a bit of rhythm in his presser. Oli McBurnie should lead the line again.

Gary O’Neil has a fully fit squad for the clash with Manchester City. Abdul Fatawu is back from suspension, too. The winger will likely come straight back into the starting XI here, potentially with Jack Clarke, leaving Jaden Philogene and Daizen Maeda’s places on the flanks vulnerable. In the midfield pivot, Exequiel Palacios in for Luis Florentino is another potential alteration. Kjell Scherpen and Jacob Greaves both recently lost their places at the back and after last week’s win over Fulham, will likely struggle to get back in this weekend. The ‘keeper and back four should remain unchanged, then.

Joe Rodon (hamstring) remains out for Leeds United, but Daniel James (back) could potentially return for Sunday’s home encounter with Manchester United. Mateo Joseph (knee) is out for the Whites, however. Leeds have been one of the easiest teams to predict this season, with this the same team that started at Arsenal last time out. The likes of Jaka Bijol, Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson may have to settle for places on the bench again, then. If Aaronson or Wilson are preferred, it’ll potentially be at the expense of Noah Okafor.

Andoni Iraola said on Thursday that it was too early to rule out any of Dominik Szoboszlai (hamstring), Alexander Isak (quad) and Cody Gakpo (ankle), and that he wanted to keep the “chance open” of a return this weekend. Ryan Gravenberch serves a one-match ban after his dismissal for two bookable offences in Gameweek 6. Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee) and Giovanni Leoni (knee) will also miss out, with Leoni targeting a return to training during the November international break. Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz had the night off in Wednesday’s Champions League tie or were limited to second-half cameos, so you’d expect – certainly the first three anyway – to return against Brentford. The main question marks surround Szoboszlai, Isak and Gakpo, with Trey Nyoni, Munoz, Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas potential inclusions if they fail to make it. Midweek hat-trick hero Bradley Barcola should start off the left regardless.

Enzo Maresca has no fresh injuries to contend with for Saturday’s home encounter with Ipswich Town. Phil Foden is back from suspension, too. It’s a very tricky Manchester City line-up to predict this week, particularly with a trip to AEK Athens up next on Tuesday. This match also follows demanding clashes with Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain. The central midfield trio subsequently feels like the hardest to predict. Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki are included here, but Ayyoub Bouaddi impressed in midweek and could feature, with Foden also in the mix. Cherki’s place in the starting XI is far from secure, then. In the wide positions, Jeremy Doku’s minutes may continue to be managed following injury, with Iliman Ndiaye and Antoine Semenyo preferred. Josko Gvardiol v Nico O’Reilly feels like a genuine 50/50 call at left-back. As for Erling Haaland, Maresca said he will probably need to give him a “rest, some days off” soon, but he is still expected to start here. A breather in Europe is perhaps more likely.

Michael Carrick said the club had moved on quickly from Lisandro Martinez’s outburst about the Manchester United hierarchy, and that he’ll be in the squad for Sunday’s trip to Leeds United. Luke Shaw (unspecified), Noussair Mazraoui (back) and Kobbie Mainoo (unspecified), who all missed out in midweek, will be assessed. Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) remain out, however. Shaw and Mainoo will surely start if fit, but with another Champions League tie on the horizon, risks may not be taken. Fernandes was deployed on the right against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday but will likely move back centrally here, potentially ousting Youri Tielemans from the ’10’. Marcus Rashford is an alternative to the wide options included here.

Matthias Jaissle is hopeful Bazoumana Traore will be fit to face Aston Villa, after he had to come off after taking a blow to his knee against Coventry earlier this week. Anthony Elanga (unknown) remains out but could re-join training next week. Back-up goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (hamstring), Tino Livramento (unspecified) and Jacob Ramsey (thigh) will also miss Gameweek 7. Dan Burn will likely have to make do with substitute duty again as he continues to build his fitness after injury, but Jaissle did say that Joelinton could make his first start of the season on Saturday. Joe Willock may have to make way to accommodate the Brazilian, with Lewis Miley another option in the engine room. Up top, Will Osula is pushing for a return. Still, Jaissle seemed to suggest Matias Fernandez-Pardo just needs a goal to get going at Newcastle, so he may be given another opportunity to lead the line here.

Oliver Glasner could be without Morgan Gibbs-White on Sunday after he picked up a minor muscle injury at Selhurst Park last week. However, he did say that he could join tomorrow’s training session and that he had a chance to feature, with the extra day of recovery potentially key. If Gibbs-White fails to make it, Callum Hudson-Odoi is the most likely player to come in. Elsewhere, Nikola Milenkovic is back in training but a start feels unlikely, given that he only recently returned. Nicolo Savona (knee) and Igor Jesus (calf) remain out. At the back, Jair Cunha could replace Ola Aina, while Ibrahim Sangare is an alternative to James McAtee, should Glasner want more physicality in the middle of the park.

Wilson Isidor (knock) is a doubt for Sunderland with a minor injury and will be assessed. Thomas Meunier (groin), Dan Ballard (hamstring) and Romaine Mundle (knee) are unavailable, however. Brian Brobbey is in contention to start on Sunday, particularly if Wilson Isidor fails to prove his fitness. The Dutchman returned to the bench for Thursday’s Europa League clash but remained unused. Trai Hume and Nilson Angulo could offer support from the flanks, with Malick Fofana another option out wide. Habib Diarra is an outside bet to start in one of the midfield positions, having recently returned from injury as a sub.

But the expectation is that the World Cup winner will get minutes off the bench, with a start more likely in the Gameweek 8 encounter with Chelsea. Archie Gray’s recent form makes that an easier decision for De Zerbi. Andrew Robertson was rested for the draw at Old Trafford following a busy international break with Scotland, and could threaten Destiny Udogie's starting role, although the Italian will likely retain his spot following a decent showing in Manchester. Mikel Arteta hopes Martin Zubimendi (unspecified) will be fit to face Nottingham Forest on Sunday, but Piero Hincapie (ankle) is still a concern, with the Spaniard saying “he will probably need another week or two”. William Saliba (back) and Christos Tzolis (hamstring) remain out. Aside from which of Ben White or Jurrien Timber gets the nod at right-back, probably the main source of debate is who joins Declan Rice in the middle of the park, with Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly the main contenders. Despite finding the net in midweek, Eberechi Eze may have to bide his time again, with Noni Madueke preferred on the left wing. Benched in Europe, Riccardo Calafiori, Martin Odegaard, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz will almost certainly be restored to the starting XI at the City Ground.

Ross Barkley (knock) and George Hemmings (knee) both face late fitness tests ahead of Saturday’s trip to St James’ Park. However, Ian Maatsen (ankle) and Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring) remain sidelined, as does long-term absentee Amadou Onana (knee). Leon Goretzka made his debut as a substitute in midweek, while Brian Madjo should also be fit and available. Neither player will trouble the starting XI, however. Victor Lindelof and Pau Torres should retain their partnership at the back after Wednesday’s clean sheet, while Joao Gomes will likely take over from Barkley in the middle of the park. Elsewhere, Ibrahim Mbaye impressed in the win over Fenerbahce and could keep his place over Emiliano Buendia, particularly with the more defensive-minded Aaron Wan-Bissaka having to cover at left-back.

Marco Rose faced the media in the aftermath of Thursday’s 3-0 win over Sturm Graz. He provided a positive update on Alex Scott (tendon), whose injury doesn’t appear to be as bad as first feared. He’ll still be out for a few weeks, mind. Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), Julian Araujo (thigh) and Eli Junior Kroupi (foot) are all reportedly back on the grass, and some could return in the next week or two. Rose has quickly settled on a favoured XI this season, with eight players featuring in every Premier League line-up. The central midfield positions have seen a bit upheaval, however, with Ryan Christie, Tyler Adams and Justin Kluivert perhaps preferred here. Kluivert – and Amine Adli – both returned to action as second half substitutes in Europe.

Kevin Schade (shoulder) and Jannik Schuster (ankle) will be assessed, after both were substituted off with issues last week. Keith Andrews also said that Nathan Collins (calf) and Mikkel Damsgaard (unspecified) could return on Saturday. That leaves Antoni Milambo (knee), Josh Dasilva (hamstring) and Kaye Furo (knee), who all remain out. With Schade a doubt, Keane Lewis-Potter could return to the left flank, having filled in centrally at Villa Park last week. Dango Ouattara is an alternative option out wide. Sepp van den Berg was back on the bench in Gameweek 6 and feels like the likely replacement for Schuster, should he miss out, although Aaron Hickey could also fill in at centre-back. If Mamadou Sangare makes his first start since Gameweek 4, Yehor Yarmoliuk or Vitaly Janelt would have to make way for that to happen.

Pascal Struijk’s ban has been overturned, but he will still need to be assessed ahead of Sunday’s derby. Fabian Hurzeler isn’t expecting anyone else back, although Mats Wieffer (knee) and Yankuba Minteh (leg) are getting close. The hope for Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) is that he will return in/around the November international break. Femi Azeez (hamstring), Zadok Yohanna (unspecified), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Stefan Tzimas (knee) remain out. As for the starting XI, we could see an unchanged lineup from Gameweek 6, with Lewis Dunk in for Struijk the likeliest change at the back. Jack Hinshelwood made his return from injury in Europe on Thursday, but a substitute role looks likely here. Georginio Rutter played 90 minutes in that match, too, which suggests Charalampos Kostoulas will get the nod against Palace.

Reece James is set to miss three months of action after undergoing knee surgery. Jamie Gittens (ankle) and Emmanuel Emegha (knock) are also out. The injury to James should mean Jordan Henderson and Moises Caicedo continue in central midfield, although Romeo Lavia is among those pushing for a recall. However, after last weekend’s 5-1 win over Bournemouth, Xabi Alonso may be tempted to name an unchanged starting XI. If he does decide to mix it up, he could perhaps pick Wesley Fofana over Josh Acheampong, while Jorrell Hato and Marco Palestra, who returned from injury last week, are alternative options at wing-back. Front three Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro will surely lead the line.

Alex Toth has joined Alex Scott (tendon) and Julian Araujo (thigh) on the injury list after suffering a hamstring injury in Thursday's win over AC Milan. Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), on the cusp of a competitive comeback, is getting game-time with the under-21s, meanwhile. Someone we could see in Gameweek 8 is Eli Junior Kroupi (foot), who hasn't featured yet in 2026/27. The young Frenchman is back in training, and while he didn't/couldn't feature against Milan (he's not in the UEFA Europa League squad), Marco Rose said that "the plan is to have him with us in Manchester". The Bournemouth boss also confirmed that Evanilson was fine after the Brazilian appeared to pick up a knock in midweek. Rose rested Rayan, Lewis Cook, Djordje Petrovic and Adam Smith on Thursday, and while he otherwise went strong with his line-up, a 2-0 lead and a numerical advantage allowed him to take off Evanilson, Marcus Tavernier and Tyler Adams early. Justin Kluivert was also substituted after an hour, with Ryan Christie lasting the course, so it's possible that the Dutchman gets the nod in the '10' at Old Trafford. He hasn't long been back from a month-long injury, however, so it remains to be seen if he can string together two starts in quick succession. Bench duty, at best, surely beckons for Kroupi.

Jannik Schuster (ankle/illness) returns to the Brentford squad this weekend, while there are no fresh injuries to report. Two Bees do have to serve bans after Gameweek 7 red cards, however: Vitaly Janelt has a one-match suspension, while Yehor Yarmolyuk begins a three-match ban. Antoni Milambo (knee), Josh Dasilva (hamstring) and Kaye Furo (knee) all remain out, meanwhile. Schuster's recovery means that Keith Andrews has a full complement of centre-halves to choose from, although the Brentford boss did point out the various stages of fitness they're at (Kristoffer Ajer the mainstay, Sepp van den Berg ahead of Nathan Collins in his recovery, and Schuster having a disrupted two weeks). How Andrews deals with the absences of Yarmolyuk and Janelt is the big question. Mamadou Sangare is surely going to replace one of them, but does the Brentford boss go bold and bring in Mikkel Damsgaard and push Mathias Jensen further back? Andrews may fear the lack of engine-room physicality against a robust Hull side, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see Aaron Hickey alongside Sangare. Another option is to move Keane Lewis-Potter into the '10' and bring in El Hadji Malick Diouf at left-back, something we saw against Aston Villa in Gameweek 6. Having been fit enough for 45 minutes against Liverpool, we'd expect to see Kevin Schade return to the starting XI at the expense of Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony.

Yankuba Minteh (leg) and Mats Wieffer (knee) are closing in on returns but this match may come too soon for the pair, with a Gameweek 9 comeback likelier. Femi Azeez (hamstring), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Zadok Yohanna (unspecified), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Stefan Tzimas (knee) also remain out, while Pascal Struijk will have a minor issue assessed after he missed the last three matches in all competitions. Jason Steele sat out Thursday's draw with Jablonec with illness but Diego Gomez and Maxim De Cuyper, also absent in Czechia, were merely rested. Fabian Hurzeler has unsurprisingly kept things very settled during this fine run of form, with 10 players starting every match they've been available for over the last five Gameweeks. The only changing of the guard has come in midfield, with Chema Andres ousting Malick Yalcouye. And Thursday's line-up was a big steer towards Sunday, with Hurzeler resting eight of his 10 starting outfielders from Gameweek 7. The two that survived, Pascal Gross and Olivier Boscagli, were taken off early. The fit-again Jack Hinshelwood is probably the one who is going to most threaten this first-choice league XI, with Yasin Ayari at risk, but bench duty likely beckons for the former again.

How Andrews deals with the absences of Yarmolyuk and Janelt is the big question. Mamadou Sangare is surely going to replace one of them, but does the Brentford boss go bold and bring in Mikkel Damsgaard and push Mathias Jensen further back? Andrews may fear the lack of engine-room physicality against a robust Hull side, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see Aaron Hickey alongside Sangare. Another option is to move Keane Lewis-Potter into the '10' and bring in El Hadji Malick Diouf at left-back, something we saw against Aston Villa in Gameweek 6. Having been fit enough for 45 minutes against Liverpool, we'd expect to see Kevin Schade return to the starting XI at the expense of Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony.

The midfielder missed Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League win over Viking with a “small injury”. Matty Cash and Ian Maatsen were preserved in midweek and should return to the full-back positions; the one question mark is over the match fitness of Maatsen, who has recently had a spell out. Boubacar Kamara is another who will almost certainly return to the side, following his Wednesday night breather. If Manzambi doesn't make it, then Unai Emery may go with Ross Barkley or Leon Goretzka, and he has sometimes opted for more conservative selections against big-six opponents in the past anyway. Tyrone Mings for Pau Torres (or Maatsen) is a very possible change to the XI you see here.

Alex Toth has joined Alex Scott (tendon) and Julian Araujo (thigh) on the injury list after suffering a hamstring injury in Thursday's win over AC Milan. Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), on the cusp of a competitive comeback, is getting game-time with the under-21s, meanwhile. Someone we could see in Gameweek 8 is Eli Junior Kroupi (foot), who hasn't featured yet in 2026/27. The young Frenchman is back in training, and while he didn't/couldn't feature against Milan (he's not in the UEFA Europa League squad), Marco Rose said that "the plan is to have him with us in Manchester". The Bournemouth boss also confirmed that Evanilson was fine after the Brazilian appeared to pick up a knock in midweek. Rose rested Rayan, Lewis Cook, Djordje Petrovic and Adam Smith on Thursday, and while he otherwise went strong with his line-up, a 2-0 lead and a numerical advantage allowed him to take off Evanilson, Marcus Tavernier and Tyler Adams early. Justin Kluivert was also substituted after an hour, with Ryan Christie lasting the course, so it's possible that the Dutchman gets the nod in the '10' at Old Trafford. He hasn't long been back from a month-long injury, however, so it remains to be seen if he can string together two starts in quick succession. Bench duty, at best, surely beckons for Kroupi.

Jannik Schuster (ankle/illness) returns to the Brentford squad this weekend, while there are no fresh injuries to report. Two Bees do have to serve bans after Gameweek 7 red cards, however: Vitaly Janelt has a one-match suspension, while Yehor Yarmolyuk begins a three-match ban. Antoni Milambo (knee), Josh Dasilva (hamstring) and Kaye Furo (knee) all remain out, meanwhile. Schuster's recovery means that Keith Andrews has a full complement of centre-halves to choose from, although the Brentford boss did point out the various stages of fitness they're at (Kristoffer Ajer the mainstay, Sepp van den Berg ahead of Nathan Collins in his recovery, and Schuster having a disrupted two weeks). How Andrews deals with the absences of Yarmolyuk and Janelt is the big question. Mamadou Sangare is surely going to replace one of them, but does the Brentford boss go bold and bring in Mikkel Damsgaard and push Mathias Jensen further back? Andrews may fear the lack of engine-room physicality against a robust Hull side, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see Aaron Hickey alongside Sangare. Another option is to move Keane Lewis-Potter into the '10' and bring in El Hadji Malick Diouf at left-back, something we saw against Aston Villa in Gameweek 6. Having been fit enough for 45 minutes against Liverpool, we'd expect to see Kevin Schade return to the starting XI at the expense of Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony.

Yankuba Minteh (leg) and Mats Wieffer (knee) are closing in on returns but this match may come too soon for the pair, with a Gameweek 9 comeback likelier. Femi Azeez (hamstring), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Zadok Yohanna (unspecified), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Stefan Tzimas (knee) also remain out, while Pascal Struijk will have a minor issue assessed after he missed the last three matches in all competitions. Jason Steele sat out Thursday's draw with Jablonec with illness but Diego Gomez and Maxim De Cuyper, also absent in Czechia, were merely rested. Fabian Hurzeler has unsurprisingly kept things very settled during this fine run of form, with 10 players starting every match they've been available for over the last five Gameweeks. The only changing of the guard has come in midfield, with Chema Andres ousting Malick Yalcouye. And Thursday's line-up was a big steer towards Sunday, with Hurzeler resting eight of his 10 starting outfielders from Gameweek 7. The two that survived, Pascal Gross and Olivier Boscagli, were taken off early. The fit-again Jack Hinshelwood is probably the one who is going to most threaten this first-choice league XI, with Yasin Ayari at risk, but bench duty likely beckons for the former again.

Emiliano Martinez will be sidelined for "weeks" after undergoing surgery on his jaw. He joins Reece James (knee), Emmanuel Emegha (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) on the sidelines, while this game comes just too soon for Pep Chavarria (muscle). Malo Gusto is back from illness, at least. Mike Penders will come in for Martinez between the sticks but you can't imagine Xabi Alonso making too many other changes, with fatigue not a concern due to a lack of midweek action and the Blues fresh from a 2-0 win over Everton. The achievement of a first clean sheet since January may also encourage Alonso to stick with the same defensive set-up (the solid midfield partnership of Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson has also helped settle things down) but the Chelsea boss sometimes struggles to resist the temptation to tinker, so you wouldn't be entirely surprised to see Wesley Fofana return to the back three or Gusto oust Jorrel Hato from the side.

Luke Woolfenden (knee), Aurele Amenda (calf), Josh Eccles (ankle) and Haji Wright (quad) will miss out once again for the Sky Blues but there were no new concerns raised in Frank Lampard's pre-match presser. Lampard declared himself happy with the performance in Monday's defeat to Tottenham Hotspur but he's shown that he's not afraid of tinkering regardless, as he proved when tweaking the winning sides sent out against Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United. Taiwo Awoniyi for Sidiki Cherif is certainly one possible alteration up top, while Frank Onyeka is putting pressure on Caleb Yirenkyi in the engine room. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto had a decent game on Monday, in what was his first ever Premier League start, so he may see off the challenge of the deposed Ephron Mason-Clark. Summer signings Loum Tchaouna and Yann Gboho appear to be even further down the attacking midfield pecking order, having been left out of the 20-man squad in Gameweek 7 in a purely tactical decision.

We haven't yet heard from Pierre Sage as the Gameweek 8 deadline draws near, with Palace's Thursday night commitments seemingly messing with the usual press conference schedule. We do know that Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) are out, while Dean Henderson (ankle) is back in training and could potentially return in Gameweek 8. What's not known is the extent of the issue that saw Quinten Timber join the injury list ahead of Thursday's UEFA Europa League tie with Besiktas. Nor do we have much information on Jorgen Strand Larsen, who came off injured in Turkey. Sage hasn't done massive amounts of tinkering between Europe and the Premier League, and you'd imagine the serious rotation will wait for next week's EFL Cup last-16 tie. The Palace boss said that Ismaila Sarr wasn’t ready to start for Palace against Besiktas, so it'll be a big jump for him to be ready to do so this weekend. Meanwhile, is Jean-Philippe Mateta able to string together two starts in less than 72 hours, having recently spent a month out? Eddie Nketiah may have to deputise.

David Moyes was coy when asked about Everton's team news for the trip to Arsenal, saying that the Toffees have their "share of bits and pieces". And he wasn't biting when asked specifically about the availability of Jarrad Branthwaite, who was missing from Thursday's training video. It should be said, however, that Vitalii Mykolenko wasn't seen in the corresponding video last week, and he did feature in Gameweek 7. Still, if there are any concerns about Branthwaite's fitness heading into the busy autumn period (he was carefully managed last season), this may be the fixture to do it, with more winnable tests ahead. Michael Keane could come in for Branthwaite if needed, while it wouldn't be a huge shock to see the Everton boss add more height to the backline against the Arsenal set-piece monsters in the shape of Jake O'Brien, especially as Ainsley Maitland-Niles has struggled at right-back of late. Christian Nørgaard won't be troubling the starting XI, as Moyes admitted that his cameo last weekend showed just how lacking in match fitness he was. So, as ever, it's the question of what Moyes is going to do on the right flank, with Brennan Johnson's four-game stint ended by Merlin Rohl last time out. Tyrique George is also an option, even if it is on his less favoured side.

Emile Smith Rowe missed out in Gameweek 7 with "some issues" but Alvaro Arbeloa says he has a fully fit squad for the trip to Coventry City, which suggests he has recovered. The Spaniard's comments also imply that Hugo Larsson has shaken off a groin problem. The Cottagers will definitely be without one player, however: Ryan Sessegnon begins a three-match ban, following his dismissal last weekend. Arbeloa has kept a very settled side over the last four Gameweeks, with his only changes - fitness-led ones, at that - coming at full-back. There's probably scant reason to change now, then, considering that Fulham ended their winless run with a deserved victory over Hull City last weekend. Gonzalo Garcia is on a six-match drought up top and Arbeloa admits that "he needs a goal," but the Cottagers' head coach said he was otherwise "happy" with the striker's wider contribution to the team. Rodrigo Muniz may have to continue to be patient, then.

Matt Targett (ankle), Jack Butland (shoulder), Charlie Hughes (groin) and Ilyas Ansah (back) remain on the sidelines, while Nobel Mendy (groin) is back on the grass but won't return until next week. Mohamed-Ali Cho (thigh) and Lucas Gourna-Douath (calf) could return, however, having trained the whole week. The latter got a kick on the same calf in training on Thursday but has trained on Friday "normally". Robinio Vaz has also escaped injury despite taking studs to the Achilles in Gameweek 7, and has trained all week. Sergej Jakirovic promised to make changes following what was the Tigers' worst display of 2026/27 against Fulham, so there's an air of uncertainty about what sort of side we'll see. It wouldn't be a huge shock to see him go back to the left-sided formula that worked well at the start of the campaign, for instance, reinstating Ryan Giles and Elliot Stroud. Joe Gelhardt is another option down the left wing. Tim Iroegbunam also seems to be inching closer to a start after coming on at half-time last weekend, with Matt Crooks potentially at risk.

Saka Lukic (groin) won't be fit for the Gameweek 8 curtain-raiser but Gary O’Neil otherwise appears to have a fully fit squad for Friday's clash with Nottingham Forest. With the Tractor Boys back on home soil, and with this fixture more 'winnable' on paper than last Saturday's trip to the Etihad, you could envisage O'Neil dropping a third centre-half (Jacob Greaves) and reinstating an attacking midfielder, i.e. Jack Clarke and/or Abdul Fatawu. Clarke v Daizen Maeda is a tough call on the left, although the latter did score last weekend and his work ethic may be preferred against Daniel Munoz and Morgan Gibbs-White down the Forest right. Luis Florentino will probably deputise again for Lukic (Azor Matusiwa is an alternative), while Zian Flemming is breathing down Emersonn's neck up front.

Daniel James (back) returns this week but Joe Rodon (hamstring) and Mateo Joseph (knee) remain out, and there's a triple whammy of fresh bad news in attack: all of Leeds' front three from Gameweek 7 are described as "major doubts". Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Anton Stach have contact injuries, while Noah Okafor has adductor issues. Daniel Farke said that, had the game been played on Friday or Saturday, none would have made it, but he did hint that the extra 24 hours may be crucial, and he does have a lot of previous for describing players as major doubts, only for them to feature. Stach and Calvert-Lewin only being affected by bruising is also potentially a positive, as there aren't the risks associated with muscle injuries. Noah Okafor, Harry Wilson and, likely, Brenden Aaronson will be on standby in the respective positions, should any of the regulars miss out. Otherwise, there's not a huge deal of debate about the XI, which has remained unchanged in Gameweeks 3-7.

Dominik Szoboszlai (hamstring) is back in individual training but won't return this weekend. Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee), Jeremie Frimpong (hamstring) and Giovanni Leoni (knee) remain out, too. Liverpool may also be without Victor Munoz for Sunday's clash with Brighton and Hove Albion. The Spaniard missed the midweek Champions League win over Villarreal thanks to a knock he picked up in Gameweek 7, and Andoni Iraola says it will be "difficult" for him to be available. Bradley Barcola, who was only in individual training on Thursday, is fine, however. Barcola, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Milos Kerkez all had welcome breathers in midweek and should return to the starting XI here, while Alexis Mac Allister, who has had managed game-time in the past, may have to go again despite back-to-back 90 minutes in the last week. A Tuesday-Sunday turnaround should help, at least. It's probably two from three of Ronald Araujo, Ryan Gravenberch and Trey Nyoni, with Gravenberch taking over right-back duties from Araujo in the second half of the seven-goal thriller with Villarreal. And it'll be Rio Ngumoha v Cody Gakpo for the one remaining spot in attack. Gakpo is only just back from injury and lasted the whole 90 minutes in the Champions League, so you'd imagine that it'd be Ngumoha, buoyed by a superb showing against the La Liga outfit, who gets the nod down the right.

Erling Haaland is “100% available” for Manchester City’s clash with Aston Villa this weekend. The Norwegian limped off after the Gameweek 7 win over Ipswich Town but made a swift recovery to make the bench in Tuesday’s thumping of AEK Athens, and is ready to start on Saturday. Enzo Maresca couldn’t, however, say for sure whether Matheus Nunes (unspecified), Mateo Kovacic (unspecified) and Nico O’Reilly (back) - who were all forced off against Ipswich - would be fit. Maresca had seemingly given them the all-clear in his pre-match presser before AEK, but they failed to show in midweek, having not trained before that. Antoine Semenyo (knee), of course, will be out until mid-December. As you’d expect, Maresca wasn’t giving anything away when it came to team selection. There was praise for Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden after their fine Champions League performances, but the City boss did say that it's "not a matter of just one game". The fact that Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku didn't kick a ball against the Greek outfit was perhaps an indication that they were being held back for Gameweek 8, while Ayyoub Bouaddi's lack of involvement was also noteworthy. Has Maresca been sufficiently spooked by Aston Villa's recent displays to revisit the more conservative tactics that sparked a comeback against PSG, specifically Bouaddi in the engine room alongside Elliot Anderson, and Enzo Fernandez pushed forward into the '10'? At the back, Abdudokir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol will be on standby

There were no team news updates in the first section of Michael Carrick's presser, which was predictably dominated by United's form, the midweek loss in Italy and talk of dressing room turmoil. There is another section to come but that won't be till well after the Gameweek 8 deadline. Of what we do know already, Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Manuel Ugarte (knee), Benjamin Sesko (calf), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Kobbie Mainoo (unspecified) will remain out. Ayden Heaven (illness), Lisandro Martinez (thigh) and Marcus Rashford (hip) all missed Wednesday’s clash with Como, meanwhile, but we could see any or all of them return, given the minor nature of their issues. Will Carrick rule with an iron fist and bench the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans following their public criticism? Or does the United boss attempt to galvanise the squad in the face of adversity and go with his 'best' players in a bid to save his job? It'll be interesting to see what he does with those two, as well as Matheus Cunha, who was hauled off at half-time in midweek. Noussair Mazraoui will be on standby to feature if Martinez doesn't recover, as you can't imagine that Matthijs de Ligt is going to start twice in quick succession after so long out. Joshua Zirkzee could get a look-in further forward if some of his outspoken teammates are consigned to the naughty step.

Anthony Elanga (unknown) has rejoined training this week and could be involved in the squad on Sunday, although Matthias Jaissle did stress that the winger wouldn't be ready for 90 minutes. The Newcastle boss added that the Magpies would take it "step by step" with Jacob Ramsey (thigh) after his own return to the grass. Ewen Jaouen (hamstring) and Tino Livramento (unspecified) remain out. Elsewhere, Mathias Fernandez-Pardo has had his week of training affected by illness. Newcastle's team is probably the hardest to guess this week, as some players are out of form, other summer signings are yet to be fully trusted with sustained game-time (Sean Steur, Bazoumana Toure), and the true match fitness of some recent returnees (Will Osula, Dan Burn and Amar Dedic) is unknown. Osula had an extended run-out as a substitute last weekend, so may be closer than the other two.

Morgan Gibbs-White (muscle) has trained all week and is available to face Ipswich Town on Friday. Nikola Milenkovic, on the bench last weekend after a bone bruise and hamstring issues, is "ready to start", too. Nicolo Savona (knee) and Igor Jesus (calf) are the only absentees, then, unless anything has happened in between Oliver Glasner's early Wednesday presser and kick-off at Portman Road. Gibbs-White, naturally, will almost certainly return to the starting XI, but Nicolas Dominguez can count himself unlucky if it's he who has to make way. At the rear, and despite what Glasner said, it's not a 100% certainty that Milenkovic returns to this side. His last competitive minutes were in early September (he did get 45 minutes in a mid-season friendly), while Ousmane Diomande is beginning to settle at centre-half after a shaky start to his Premier League career. It wasn't a bad defensive performance from Forest against Arsenal last weekend, either.

We haven't yet heard from Regis Le Bris as the Gameweek 8 deadline hurtles towards us, with Sunderland's Thursday night commitments messing with the usual press conference schedule. The last we heard, Brian Brobbey (hamstring) was seemingly being held back for this weekend, having trained for the last 10 days but not been risked against Bournemouth or Lech Poznan. Wilson Isidor (knock) and Thomas Meunier (groin) were only in individual training at the point of the last update, however, while Dan Ballard (hamstring) and Romaine Mundle (knee) are most definitely out. Kevin Danso also serves a one-match ban. Whether Brobbey is fit enough to start is another question, so Timur Tutyerov may have to lead the line instead, at least from kick-off. Who partners Nordi Mukiele is another source of debate, with Omar Alderete in a really bad spell of form; Luke O'Nien may well have edged back above him in the pecking order now. Nilson Angulo impressed down the right flank on Thursday and may get the nod there again, and the fact that he and Habib Diarra were taken off early, at the same time as fellow regulars Granit Xhaka and Mukiele, does hint at them possibly being saved for Leeds. Chris Rigg is another option on the right.

Pedro Porro (hamstring) returns this weekend but Lucas Bergvall (knee), Destiny Udogie (knee), Savinho (muscle), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain out. Rodrigo Bentancur is still suspended, too. Andrew Robertson and Omar Marmoush are fine despite appearing to limp off on Monday but Roberto De Zerbi is not sure whether previous long-term absentees James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski will feature, with the pair restricted to individual training in the aftermath of the Coventry game. Kulusevski wouldn't have started anyway but it wouldn't be a shock to see Conor Gallagher come in for Maddison for this tricky away game, whether that's in the back-three system De Zerbi used in Gameweek 7 or in a more conventional 4-2-3-1. Matheus Fernandes is another option. Porro hasn't featured much since early September, meanwhile, so you wonder if he'll be eased in.

Mikel Arteta wasn't able to give us a timeline on Bukayo Saka after the midfielder came off with a quad injury in Wednesday's draw with Bayern Munich. It's fair to say, though, that he's going to miss this weekend, and likely more games beyond it. William Saliba (back) and Christos Tzolis (hamstring) also remain out but Piero Hincapie (ankle) has rejoined training this week and is available. You'd expect Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze to be stationed down the flanks in the absence of Saka and Tzolis, while Arteta will surely push his overworked regulars through one more match before making wholesale changes against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday. Riccardo Calafiori is someone whose game-time has been monitored in the past but Arteta encouragingly said on Friday that the Italian "is in a different place" this term "because he had a full pre-season", adding that he's "ready" to go again. Ben White should return as the regular rotation continues at right-back, while there's a chance we may see Myles Lewis-Skelly come back into midfield, with Bruno Guimaraes perhaps still not quite at top fitness and form. Kai Havertz's own displays have dipped recently, so it's not out of the question that Viktor Gyokeres features against the Toffees.

Rodrigo Muniz may have to continue to be patient, then.

Matt Targett (ankle), Jack Butland (shoulder), Charlie Hughes (groin) and Ilyas Ansah (back) remain on the sidelines, while Nobel Mendy (groin) is back on the grass but won't return until next week. Joe Gelhardt is another option down the left wing. Tim Iroegbunam also seems to be inching closer to a start after coming on at half-time last weekend, with Matt Crooks potentially at risk.

Otherwise, there's not a huge deal of debate about the XI, which has remained unchanged in Gameweeks 3-7.

Dominik Szoboszlai (hamstring) is back in individual training but won't return this weekend. Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee), Jeremie Frimpong (hamstring) and Giovanni Leoni (knee) remain out, too. Liverpool may also be without Victor Munoz for Sunday's clash with Brighton and Hove Albion. The Spaniard missed the midweek Champions League win over Villarreal thanks to a knock he picked up in Gameweek 7, and Andoni Iraola says it will be "difficult" for him to be available. Bradley Barcola, who was only in individual training on Thursday, is fine, however. Barcola, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Milos Kerkez all had welcome breathers in midweek and should return to the starting XI here, while Alexis Mac Allister, who has had managed game-time in the past, may have to go again despite back-to-back 90 minutes in the last week. A Tuesday-Sunday turnaround should help, at least. It's probably two from three of Ronald Araujo, Ryan Gravenberch and Trey Nyoni, with Gravenberch taking over right-back duties from Araujo in the second half of the seven-goal thriller with Villarreal. And it'll be Rio Ngumoha v Cody Gakpo for the one remaining spot in attack. Gakpo is only just back from injury and lasted the whole 90 minutes in the Champions League, so you'd imagine that it'd be Ngumoha, buoyed by a superb showing against the La Liga outfit, who gets the nod down the right.

Has Maresca been sufficiently spooked by Aston Villa's recent displays to revisit the more conservative tactics that sparked a comeback against PSG, specifically Bouaddi in the engine room alongside Elliot Anderson, and Enzo Fernandez pushed forward into the '10'? At the back, Abdudokir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol will be on standby

Osula had an extended run-out as a substitute last weekend, so may be closer than the other two.

Morgan Gibbs-White (muscle) has trained all week and is available to face Ipswich Town on Friday. Nikola Milenkovic, on the bench last weekend after a bone bruise and hamstring issues, is "ready to start", too. Nicolo Savona (knee) and Igor Jesus (calf) are the only absentees, then, unless anything has happened in between Oliver Glasner's early Wednesday presser and kick-off at Portman Road. Gibbs-White, naturally, will almost certainly return to the starting XI, but Nicolas Dominguez can count himself unlucky if it's he who has to make way. At the rear, and despite what Glasner said, it's not a 100% certainty that Milenkovic returns to this side. His last competitive minutes were in early September (he did get 45 minutes in a mid-season friendly), while Ousmane Diomande is beginning to settle at centre-half after a shaky start to his Premier League career. It wasn't a bad defensive performance from Forest against Arsenal last weekend, either.

We haven't yet heard from Regis Le Bris as the Gameweek 8 deadline hurtles towards us, with Sunderland's Thursday night commitments messing with the usual press conference schedule. The last we heard, Brian Brobbey (hamstring) was seemingly being held back for this weekend, having trained for the last 10 days but not been risked against Bournemouth or Lech Poznan. Wilson Isidor (knock) and Thomas Meunier (groin) were only in individual training at the point of the last update, however, while Dan Ballard (hamstring) and Romaine Mundle (knee) are most definitely out. Kevin Danso also serves a one-match ban. Whether Brobbey is fit enough to start is another question, so Timur Tutyerov may have to lead the line instead, at least from kick-off. Who partners Nordi Mukiele is another source of debate, with Omar Alderete in a really bad spell of form; Luke O'Nien may well have edged back above him in the pecking order now. Nilson Angulo impressed down the right flank on Thursday and may get the nod there again, and the fact that he and Habib Diarra were taken off early, at the same time as fellow regulars Granit Xhaka and Mukiele, does hint at them possibly being saved for Leeds. Chris Rigg is another option on the right.

Pedro Porro (hamstring) returns this weekend but Lucas Bergvall (knee), Destiny Udogie (knee), Savinho (muscle), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain out. Rodrigo Bentancur is still suspended, too. Andrew Robertson and Omar Marmoush are fine despite appearing to limp off on Monday but Roberto De Zerbi is not sure whether previous long-term absentees James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski will feature, with the pair restricted to individual training in the aftermath of the Coventry game. Kulusevski wouldn't have started anyway but it wouldn't be a shock to see Conor Gallagher come in for Maddison for this tricky away game, whether that's in the back-three system De Zerbi used in Gameweek 7 or in a more conventional 4-2-3-1. Matheus Fernandes is another option. Porro hasn't featured much since early September, meanwhile, so you wonder if he'll be eased in.

Mikel Arteta wasn't able to give us a timeline on Bukayo Saka after the midfielder came off with a quad injury in Wednesday's draw with Bayern Munich. It's fair to say, though, that he's going to miss this weekend, and likely more games beyond it. William Saliba (back) and Christos Tzolis (hamstring) also remain out but Piero Hincapie (ankle) has rejoined training this week and is available. You'd expect Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze to be stationed down the flanks in the absence of Saka and Tzolis, while Arteta will surely push his overworked regulars through one more match before making wholesale changes against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday. Riccardo Calafiori is someone whose game-time has been monitored in the past but Arteta encouragingly said on Friday that the Italian "is in a different place" this term "because he had a full pre-season", adding that he's "ready" to go again. Ben White should return as the regular rotation continues at right-back, while there's a chance we may see Myles Lewis-Skelly come back into midfield, with Bruno Guimaraes perhaps still not quite at top fitness and form. Kai Havertz's own displays have dipped recently, so it's not out of the question that Viktor Gyokeres features against the Toffees.

Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (hamstring) and Amadou Onana (knee) remain out, while Johan Manzambi faces a fitness test ahead of Aston Villa’s clash with Manchester City. The midfielder missed Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League win over Viking with a “small injury”. Matty Cash and Ian Maatsen were preserved in midweek and should return to the full-back positions; the one question mark is over the match fitness of Maatsen, who has recently had a spell out. Boubacar Kamara is another who will almost certainly return to the side, following his Wednesday night breather. If Manzambi doesn't make it, then Unai Emery may go with Ross Barkley or Leon Goretzka, and he has sometimes opted for more conservative selections against big-six opponents in the past anyway. Tyrone Mings for Pau Torres (or Maatsen) is a very possible change to the XI you see here.

Alex Toth has joined Alex Scott (tendon) and Julian Araujo (thigh) on the injury list after suffering a hamstring injury in Thursday's win over AC Milan. Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), on the cusp of a competitive comeback, is getting game-time with the under-21s, meanwhile. Someone we could see in Gameweek 8 is Eli Junior Kroupi (foot), who hasn't featured yet in 2026/27. The young Frenchman is back in training, and while he didn't/couldn't feature against Milan (he's not in the UEFA Europa League squad), Marco Rose said that "the plan is to have him with us in Manchester". The Bournemouth boss also confirmed that Evanilson was fine after the Brazilian appeared to pick up a knock in midweek. Rose rested Rayan, Lewis Cook, Djordje Petrovic and Adam Smith on Thursday, and while he otherwise went strong with his line-up, a 2-0 lead and a numerical advantage allowed him to take off Evanilson, Marcus Tavernier and Tyler Adams early. Justin Kluivert was also substituted after an hour, with Ryan Christie lasting the course, so it's possible that the Dutchman gets the nod in the '10' at Old Trafford. He hasn't long been back from a month-long injury, however, so it remains to be seen if he can string together two starts in quick succession. Bench duty, at best, surely beckons for Kroupi.

Jannik Schuster (ankle/illness) returns to the Brentford squad this weekend, while there are no fresh injuries to report. Two Bees do have to serve bans after Gameweek 7 red cards, however: Vitaly Janelt has a one-match suspension, while Yehor Yarmolyuk begins a three-match ban. Antoni Milambo (knee), Josh Dasilva (hamstring) and Kaye Furo (knee) all remain out, meanwhile. Schuster's recovery means that Keith Andrews has a full complement of centre-halves to choose from, although the Brentford boss did point out the various stages of fitness they're at (Kristoffer Ajer the mainstay, Sepp van den Berg ahead of Nathan Collins in his recovery, and Schuster having a disrupted two weeks). How Andrews deals with the absences of Yarmolyuk and Janelt is the big question. Mamadou Sangare is surely going to replace one of them, but does the Brentford boss go bold and bring in Mikkel Damsgaard and push Mathias Jensen further back? Andrews may fear the lack of engine-room physicality against a robust Hull side, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see Aaron Hickey alongside Sangare. Another option is to move Keane Lewis-Potter into the '10' and bring in El Hadji Malick Diouf at left-back, something we saw against Aston Villa in Gameweek 6. Having been fit enough for 45 minutes against Liverpool, we'd expect to see Kevin Schade return to the starting XI at the expense of Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony.

Yankuba Minteh (leg) and Mats Wieffer (knee) are closing in on returns but this match may come too soon for the pair, with a Gameweek 9 comeback likelier. Femi Azeez (hamstring), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Zadok Yohanna (unspecified), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Stefan Tzimas (knee) also remain out, while Pascal Struijk will have a minor issue assessed after he missed the last three matches in all competitions. Jason Steele sat out Thursday's draw with Jablonec with illness but Diego Gomez and Maxim De Cuyper, also absent in Czechia, were merely rested. Fabian Hurzeler has unsurprisingly kept things very settled during this fine run of form, with 10 players starting every match they've been available for over the last five Gameweeks. The only changing of the guard has come in midfield, with Chema Andres ousting Malick Yalcouye. And Thursday's line-up was a big steer towards Sunday, with Hurzeler resting eight of his 10 starting outfielders from Gameweek 7. The two that survived, Pascal Gross and Olivier Boscagli, were taken off early. The fit-again Jack Hinshelwood is probably the one who is going to most threaten this first-choice league XI, with Yasin Ayari at risk, but bench duty likely beckons for the former again.

Emiliano Martinez will be sidelined for "weeks" after undergoing surgery on his jaw. He joins Reece James (knee), Emmanuel Emegha (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) on the sidelines, while this game comes just too soon for Pep Chavarria (muscle). Malo Gusto is back from illness, at least. Mike Penders will come in for Martinez between the sticks but you can't imagine Xabi Alonso making too many other changes, with fatigue not a concern due to a lack of midweek action and the Blues fresh from a 2-0 win over Everton. The achievement of a first clean sheet since January may also encourage Alonso to stick with the same defensive set-up (the solid midfield partnership of Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson has also helped settle things down) but the Chelsea boss sometimes struggles to resist the temptation to tinker, so you wouldn't be entirely surprised to see Wesley Fofana return to the back three or Gusto oust Jorrel Hato from the side.

Luke Woolfenden (knee), Aurele Amenda (calf), Josh Eccles (ankle) and Haji Wright (quad) will miss out once again for the Sky Blues but there were no new concerns raised in Frank Lampard's pre-match presser. Lampard declared himself happy with the performance in Monday's defeat to Tottenham Hotspur but he's shown that he's not afraid of tinkering regardless, as he proved when tweaking the winning sides sent out against Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United. Taiwo Awoniyi for Sidiki Cherif is certainly one possible alteration up top, while Frank Onyeka is putting pressure on Caleb Yirenkyi in the engine room. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto had a decent game on Monday, in what was his first ever Premier League start, so he may see off the challenge of the deposed Ephron Mason-Clark. Summer signings Loum Tchaouna and Yann Gboho appear to be even further down the attacking midfield pecking order, having been left out of the 20-man squad in Gameweek 7 in a purely tactical decision.

We haven't yet heard from Pierre Sage as the Gameweek 8 deadline draws near, with Palace's Thursday night commitments seemingly messing with the usual press conference schedule. We do know that Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) are out, while Dean Henderson (ankle) is back in training and could potentially return in Gameweek 8. What's not known is the extent of the issue that saw Quinten Timber join the injury list ahead of Thursday's UEFA Europa League tie with Besiktas. Nor do we have much information on Jorgen Strand Larsen, who came off injured in Turkey. Sage hasn't done massive amounts of tinkering between Europe and the Premier League, and you'd imagine the serious rotation will wait for next week's EFL Cup last-16 tie. The Palace boss said that Ismaila Sarr wasn’t ready to start for Palace against Besiktas, so it'll be a big jump for him to be ready to do so this weekend. Meanwhile, is Jean-Philippe Mateta able to string together two starts in less than 72 hours, having recently spent a month out? Eddie Nketiah may have to deputise.

David Moyes was coy when asked about Everton's team news for the trip to Arsenal, saying that the Toffees have their "share of bits and pieces". And he wasn't biting when asked specifically about the availability of Jarrad Branthwaite, who was missing from Thursday's training video. It should be said, however, that Vitalii Mykolenko wasn't seen in the corresponding video last week, and he did feature in Gameweek 7. Still, if there are any concerns about Branthwaite's fitness heading into the busy autumn period (he was carefully managed last season), this may be the fixture to do it, with more winnable tests ahead. Michael Keane could come in for Branthwaite if needed, while it wouldn't be a huge shock to see the Everton boss add more height to the backline against the Arsenal set-piece monsters in the shape of Jake O'Brien, especially as Ainsley Maitland-Niles has struggled at right-back of late. Christian Nørgaard won't be troubling the starting XI, as Moyes admitted that his cameo last weekend showed just how lacking in match fitness he was. Nikola Milenkovic, on the bench last weekend after a bone bruise and hamstring issues, is "ready to start", too. At the rear, and despite what Glasner said, it's not a 100% certainty that Milenkovic returns to this side. His last competitive minutes were in early September (he did get 45 minutes in a mid-season friendly), while Ousmane Diomande is beginning to settle at centre-half after a shaky start to his Premier League career. It wasn't a bad defensive performance from Forest against Arsenal last weekend, either.

Chris Rigg is another option on the right.

Pedro Porro (hamstring) returns this weekend but Lucas Bergvall (knee), Destiny Udogie (knee), Savinho (muscle), Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle), Xavi Simons (knee) and Wilson Odobert (knee) remain out. Rodrigo Bentancur is still suspended, too. Andrew Robertson and Omar Marmoush are fine despite appearing to limp off on Monday but Roberto De Zerbi is not sure whether previous long-term absentees James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski will feature, with the pair restricted to individual training in the aftermath of the Coventry game. Kulusevski wouldn't have started anyway but it wouldn't be a shock to see Conor Gallagher come in for Maddison for this tricky away game, whether that's in the back-three system De Zerbi used in Gameweek 7 or in a more conventional 4-2-3-1. It's fair to say, though, that he's going to miss this weekend, and likely more games beyond it. William Saliba (back) and Christos Tzolis (hamstring) also remain out but Piero Hincapie (ankle) has rejoined training this week and is available. Ben White should return as the regular rotation continues at right-back, while there's a chance we may see Myles Lewis-Skelly come back into midfield, with Bruno Guimaraes perhaps still not quite at top fitness and form. Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (hamstring) and Amadou Onana (knee) remain out, while Johan Manzambi faces a fitness test ahead of Aston Villa’s clash with Manchester City. The midfielder missed Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League win over Viking with a “small injury”. Matty Cash and Ian Maatsen were preserved in midweek and should return to the full-back positions; the one question mark is over the match fitness of Maatsen, who has recently had a spell out. Boubacar Kamara is another who will almost certainly return to the side, following his Wednesday night breather. If Manzambi doesn't make it, then Unai Emery may go with Ross Barkley or Leon Goretzka, and he has sometimes opted for more conservative selections against big-six opponents in the past anyway. Tyrone Mings for Pau Torres (or Maatsen) is a very possible change to the XI you see here.

Alex Toth has joined Alex Scott (tendon) and Julian Araujo (thigh) on the injury list after suffering a hamstring injury in Thursday's win over AC Milan. Veljko Milosavljevic (knee), on the cusp of a competitive comeback, is getting game-time with the under-21s, meanwhile. Someone we could see in Gameweek 8 is Eli Junior Kroupi (foot), who hasn't featured yet in 2026/27. The young Frenchman is back in training, and while he didn't/couldn't feature against Milan (he's not in the UEFA Europa League squad), Marco Rose said that "the plan is to have him with us in Manchester". The Bournemouth boss also confirmed that Evanilson was fine after the Brazilian appeared to pick up a knock in midweek. Rose rested Rayan, Lewis Cook, Djordje Petrovic and Adam Smith on Thursday, and while he otherwise went strong with his line-up, a 2-0 lead and a numerical advantage allowed him to take off Evanilson, Marcus Tavernier and Tyler Adams early. Justin Kluivert was also substituted after an hour, with Ryan Christie lasting the course, so it's possible that the Dutchman gets the nod in the '10' at Old Trafford. He hasn't long been back from a month-long injury, however, so it remains to be seen if he can string together two starts in quick succession. Bench duty, at best, surely beckons for Kroupi.

Jannik Schuster (ankle/illness) returns to the Brentford squad this weekend, while there are no fresh injuries to report. Two Bees do have to serve bans after Gameweek 7 red cards, however: Vitaly Janelt has a one-match suspension, while Yehor Yarmolyuk begins a three-match ban. Antoni Milambo (knee), Josh Dasilva (hamstring) and Kaye Furo (knee) all remain out, meanwhile. Schuster's recovery means that Keith Andrews has a full complement of centre-halves to choose from, although the Brentford boss did point out the various stages of fitness they're at (Kristoffer Ajer the mainstay, Sepp van den Berg ahead of Nathan Collins in his recovery, and Schuster having a disrupted two weeks). How Andrews deals with the absences of Yarmolyuk and Janelt is the big question. Mamadou Sangare is surely going to replace one of them, but does the Brentford boss go bold and bring in Mikkel Damsgaard and push Mathias Jensen further back? Andrews may fear the lack of engine-room physicality against a robust Hull side, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see Aaron Hickey alongside Sangare. Another option is to move Keane Lewis-Potter into the '10' and bring in El Hadji Malick Diouf at left-back, something we saw against Aston Villa in Gameweek 6. Having been fit enough for 45 minutes against Liverpool, we'd expect to see Kevin Schade return to the starting XI at the expense of Dango Ouattara or Jaidon Anthony.

Femi Azeez (hamstring), Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring), Zadok Yohanna (unspecified), Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Stefan Tzimas (knee) also remain out, while Pascal Struijk will have a minor issue assessed after he missed the last three matches in all competitions. Jason Steele sat out Thursday's draw with Jablonec with illness but Diego Gomez and Maxim De Cuyper, also absent in Czechia, were merely rested. Fabian Hurzeler has unsurprisingly kept things very settled during this fine run of form, with 10 players starting every match they've been available for over the last five Gameweeks. The only changing of the guard has come in midfield, with Chema Andres ousting Malick Yalcouye. And Thursday's line-up was a big steer towards Sunday, with Hurzeler resting eight of his 10 starting outfielders from Gameweek 7. The two that survived, Pascal Gross and Olivier Boscagli, were taken off early. The fit-again Jack Hinshelwood is probably the one who is going to most threaten this first-choice league XI, with Yasin Ayari at risk, but bench duty likely beckons for the former again.

Emiliano Martinez will be sidelined for "weeks" after undergoing surgery on his jaw. He joins Reece James (knee), Emmanuel Emegha (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) on the sidelines, while this game comes just too soon for Pep Chavarria (muscle). Malo Gusto is back from illness, at least. Mike Penders will come in for Martinez between the sticks but you can't imagine Xabi Alonso making too many other changes, with fatigue not a concern due to a lack of midweek action and the Blues fresh from a 2-0 win over Everton. The achievement of a first clean sheet since January may also encourage Alonso to stick with the same defensive set-up (the solid midfield partnership of Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson has also helped settle things down) but the Chelsea boss sometimes struggles to resist the temptation to tinker, so you wouldn't be entirely surprised to see Wesley Fofana return to the back three or Gusto oust Jorrel Hato from the side.

Luke Woolfenden (knee), Aurele Amenda (calf), Josh Eccles (ankle) and Haji Wright (quad) will miss out once again for the Sky Blues but there were no new concerns raised in Frank Lampard's pre-match presser. Lampard declared himself happy with the performance in Monday's defeat to Tottenham Hotspur but he's shown that he's not afraid of tinkering regardless, as he proved when tweaking the winning sides sent out against Nottingham Forest and Newcastle United. Taiwo Awoniyi for Sidiki Cherif is certainly one possible alteration up top, while Frank Onyeka is putting pressure on Caleb Yirenkyi in the engine room. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto had a decent game on Monday, in what was his first ever Premier League start, so he may see off the challenge of the deposed Ephron Mason-Clark. Summer signings Loum Tchaouna and Yann Gboho appear to be even further down the attacking midfield pecking order, having been left out of the 20-man squad in Gameweek 7 in a purely tactical decision.

We haven't yet heard from Pierre Sage as the Gameweek 8 deadline draws near, with Palace's Thursday night commitments seemingly messing with the usual press conference schedule. We do know that Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) are out, while Dean Henderson (ankle) is back in training and could potentially return in Gameweek 8. What's not known is the extent of the issue that saw Quinten Timber join the injury list ahead of Thursday's UEFA Europa League tie with Besiktas. Nor do we have much information on Jorgen Strand Larsen, who came off injured in Turkey. Sage hasn't done massive amounts of tinkering between Europe and the Premier League, and you'd imagine the serious rotation will wait for next week's EFL Cup last-16 tie. The Palace boss said that Ismaila Sarr wasn’t ready to start for Palace against Besiktas, so it'll be a big jump for him to be ready to do so this weekend. Meanwhile, is Jean-Philippe Mateta able to string together two starts in less than 72 hours, having recently spent a month out? Eddie Nketiah may have to deputise.

David Moyes was coy when asked about Everton's team news for the trip to Arsenal, saying that the Toffees have their "share of bits and pieces". And he wasn't biting when asked specifically about the availability of Jarrad Branthwaite, who was missing from Thursday's training video. It should be said, however, that Vitalii Mykolenko wasn't seen in the corresponding video last week, and he did feature in Gameweek 7. Still, if there are any concerns about Branthwaite's fitness heading into the busy autumn period (he was carefully managed last season), this may be the fixture to do it, with more winnable tests ahead. Michael Keane could come in for Branthwaite if needed, while it wouldn't be a huge shock to see the Everton boss add more height to the backline against the Arsenal set-piece monsters in the shape of Jake O'Brien, especially as Ainsley Maitland-Niles has struggled at right-back of late. Christian Nørgaard won't be troubling the starting XI, as Moyes admitted that his cameo last weekend showed just how lacking in match fitness he was. So, as ever, it's the question of what Moyes is going to do on the right flank, with Brennan Johnson's four-game stint ended by Merlin Rohl last time out. Tyrique George is also an option, even if it is on his less favoured side.

Emile Smith Rowe missed out in Gameweek 7 with "some issues" but Alvaro Arbeloa says he has a fully fit squad for the trip to Coventry City, which suggests he has recovered. The Spaniard's comments also imply that Hugo Larsson has shaken off a groin problem. The Cottagers will definitely be without one player, however: Ryan Sessegnon begins a three-match ban, following his dismissal last weekend. Arbeloa has kept a very settled side over the last four Gameweeks, with his only changes - fitness-led ones, at that - coming at full-back. There's probably scant reason to change now, then, considering that Fulham ended their winless run with a deserved victory over Hull City last weekend. Gonzalo Garcia is on a six-match drought up top and Arbeloa admits that "he needs a goal," but the Cottagers' head coach said he was otherwise "happy" with the striker's wider contribution to the team. Rodrigo Muniz may have to continue to be patient, then.

Matt Targett (ankle), Jack Butland (shoulder), Charlie Hughes (groin) and Ilyas Ansah (back) remain on the sidelines, while Nobel Mendy (groin) is back on the grass but won't return until next week. Mohamed-Ali Cho (thigh) and Lucas Gourna-Douath (calf) could return, however, having trained the whole week. The latter got a kick on the same calf in training on Thursday but has trained on Friday "normally". Robinio Vaz has also escaped injury despite taking studs to the Achilles in Gameweek 7, and has trained all week. Sergej Jakirovic promised to make changes following what was the Tigers' worst display of 2026/27 against Fulham, so there's an air of uncertainty about what sort of side we'll see. It wouldn't be a huge shock to see him go back to the left-sided formula that worked well at the start of the campaign, for instance, reinstating Ryan Giles and Elliot Stroud. Joe Gelhardt is another option down the left wing. Tim Iroegbunam also seems to be inching closer to a start after coming on at half-time last weekend, with Matt Crooks potentially at risk.

Saka Lukic (groin) won't be fit for the Gameweek 8 curtain-raiser but Gary O’Neil otherwise appears to have a fully fit squad for Friday's clash with Nottingham Forest. With the Tractor Boys back on home soil, and with this fixture more 'winnable' on paper than last Saturday's trip to the Etihad, you could envisage O'Neil dropping a third centre-half (Jacob Greaves) and reinstating an attacking midfielder, i.e. Jack Clarke and/or Abdul Fatawu. Clarke v Daizen Maeda is a tough call on the left, although the latter did score last weekend and his work ethic may be preferred against Daniel Munoz and Morgan Gibbs-White down the Forest right. Luis Florentino will probably deputise again for Lukic (Azor Matusiwa is an alternative), while Zian Flemming is breathing down Emersonn's neck up front.

Daniel James (back) returns this week but Joe Rodon (hamstring) and Mateo Joseph (knee) remain out, and there's a triple whammy of fresh bad news in attack: all of Leeds' front three from Gameweek 7 are described as "major doubts". Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Anton Stach have contact injuries, while Noah Okafor has adductor issues. Daniel Farke said that, had the game been played on Friday or Saturday, none would have made it, but he did hint that the extra 24 hours may be crucial, and he does have a lot of previous for describing players as major doubts, only for them to feature. Stach and Calvert-Lewin only being affected by bruising is also potentially a positive, as there aren't the risks associated with muscle injuries. Noah Okafor, Harry Wilson and, likely, Brenden Aaronson will be on standby in the respective positions, should any of the regulars miss out. Otherwise, there's not a huge deal of debate about the XI, which has remained unchanged in Gameweeks 3-7.

Dominik Szoboszlai (hamstring) is back in individual training but won't return this weekend. Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Conor Bradley (knee), Jeremie Frimpong (hamstring) and Giovanni Leoni (knee) remain out, too. Liverpool may also be without Victor Munoz for Sunday's clash with Brighton and Hove Albion. The Spaniard missed the midweek Champions League win over Villarreal thanks to a knock he picked up in Gameweek 7, and Andoni Iraola says it will be "difficult" for him to be available. Bradley Barcola, who was only in individual training on Thursday, is fine, however. Barcola, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Milos Kerkez all had welcome breathers in midweek and should return to the starting XI here, while Alexis Mac Allister, who has had managed game-time in the past, may have to go again despite back-to-back 90 minutes in the last week. A Tuesday-Sunday turnaround should help, at least. It's probably two from three of Ronald Araujo, Ryan Gravenberch and Trey Nyoni, with Gravenberch taking over right-back duties from Araujo in the second half of the seven-goal thriller with Villarreal. And it'll be Rio Ngumoha v Cody Gakpo for the one remaining spot in attack. Gakpo is only just back from injury and lasted the whole 90 minutes in the Champions League, so you'd imagine that it'd be Ngumoha, buoyed by a superb showing against the La Liga outfit, who gets the nod down the right.

Erling Haaland is “100% available” for Manchester City’s clash with Aston Villa this weekend. The Norwegian limped off after the Gameweek 7 win over Ipswich Town but made a swift recovery to make the bench in Tuesday’s thumping of AEK Athens, and is ready to start on Saturday. Enzo Maresca couldn’t, however, say for sure whether Matheus Nunes (unspecified), Mateo Kovacic (unspecified) and Nico O’Reilly (back) - who were all forced off against Ipswich - would be fit. Maresca had seemingly given them the all-clear in his pre-match presser before AEK, but they failed to show in midweek, having not trained before that. Antoine Semenyo (knee), of course, will be out until mid-December. As you’d expect, Maresca wasn’t giving anything away when it came to team selection. There was praise for Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden after their fine Champions League performances, but the City boss did say that it's "not a matter of just one game". The fact that Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku didn't kick a ball against the Greek outfit was perhaps an indication that they were being held back for Gameweek 8, while Ayyoub Bouaddi's lack of involvement was also noteworthy. Has Maresca been sufficiently spooked by Aston Villa's recent displays to revisit the more conservative tactics that sparked a comeback against PSG, specifically Bouaddi in the engine room alongside Elliot Anderson, and Enzo Fernandez pushed forward into the '10'? At the back, Abdudokir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol will be on standby

There were no team news updates in the first section of Michael Carrick's presser, which was predictably dominated by United's form, the midweek loss in Italy and talk of dressing room turmoil. There is another section to come but that won't be till well after the Gameweek 8 deadline. Of what we do know already, Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Manuel Ugarte (knee), Benjamin Sesko (calf), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Kobbie Mainoo (unspecified) will remain out. Ayden Heaven (illness), Lisandro Martinez (thigh) and Marcus Rashford (hip) all missed Wednesday’s clash with Como, meanwhile, but we could see any or all of them return, given the minor nature of their issues. Will Carrick rule with an iron fist and bench the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans following their public criticism? Or does the United boss attempt to galvanise the squad in the face of adversity and go with his 'best' players in a bid to save his job? It'll be interesting to see what he does with those two, as well as Matheus Cunha, who was hauled off at half-time in midweek. Noussair Mazraoui will be on standby to feature if Martinez doesn't recover, as you can't imagine that Matthijs de Ligt is going to start twice in quick succession after so long out. Joshua Zirkzee could get a look-in further forward if some of his outspoken teammates are consigned to the naughty step.

Anthony Elanga (unknown) has rejoined training this week and could be involved in the squad on Sunday, although Matthias Jaissle did stress that the winger wouldn't be ready for 90 minutes. The Newcastle boss added that the Magpies would take it "step by step" with Jacob Ramsey (thigh) after his own return to the grass. Ewen Jaouen (hamstring) and Tino Livramento (unspecified) remain out. Elsewhere, Mathias Fernandez-Pardo has had his week of training affected by illness. Newcastle's team is probably the hardest to guess this week, as some players are out of form, other summer signings are yet to be fully trusted with sustained game-time (Sean Steur, Bazoumana Toure), and the true match fitness of some recent returnees (Will Osula, Dan Burn and Amar Dedic) is unknown. Osula had an extended run-out as a substitute last weekend, so may be closer than the other two.
